218#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
219// Utility function to Open File for Writing
220static FILE* OpenFileForWriting(const std::string& output_file) {
221 FILE* fileout = nullptr;
222 FilePath output_file_path(output_file);
223 FilePath output_dir(output_file_path.RemoveFileName());
224
225 if (output_dir.CreateDirectoriesRecursively()) {
226 fileout = posix::FOpen(output_file.c_str(), "w");
227 }
228 if (fileout == nullptr) {
229 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Unable to open file \"" << output_file << "\"";
230 }
231 return fileout;
232}
233#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM

237// Bazel passes in the argument to '--test_filter' via the TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY
238// environment variable.
239static const char* GetDefaultFilter() {
240 const char* const testbridge_test_only =
241 internal::posix::GetEnv("TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY");
242 if (testbridge_test_only != nullptr) {
243 return testbridge_test_only;
244 }
245 return kUniversalFilter;
246}
247
248// Bazel passes in the argument to '--test_runner_fail_fast' via the
249// TESTBRIDGE_TEST_RUNNER_FAIL_FAST environment variable.
250static bool GetDefaultFailFast() {
251 const char* const testbridge_test_runner_fail_fast =
252 internal::posix::GetEnv("TESTBRIDGE_TEST_RUNNER_FAIL_FAST");
253 if (testbridge_test_runner_fail_fast != nullptr) {
254 return strcmp(testbridge_test_runner_fail_fast, "1") == 0;
255 }
256 return false;
257}

419const uint32_t Random::kMaxRange;
420
421// Generates a random number from [0, range), using a Linear
422// Congruential Generator (LCG). Crashes if 'range' is 0 or greater
423// than kMaxRange.
424uint32_t Random::Generate(uint32_t range) {
425 // These constants are the same as are used in glibc's rand(3).
426 // Use wider types than necessary to prevent unsigned overflow diagnostics.
427 state_ = static_cast<uint32_t>(1103515245ULL * state_ + 12345U) % kMaxRange;
428
429 GTEST_CHECK_(range > 0) << "Cannot generate a number in the range [0, 0).";
430 GTEST_CHECK_(range <= kMaxRange)
431 << "Generation of a number in [0, " << range << ") was requested, "
432 << "but this can only generate numbers in [0, " << kMaxRange << ").";
433
434 // Converting via modulus introduces a bit of downward bias, but
435 // it's simple, and a linear congruential generator isn't too good
436 // to begin with.
437 return state_ % range;
438}

445// Iterates over a vector of TestSuites, keeping a running sum of the
446// results of calling a given int-returning method on each.
447// Returns the sum.
448static int SumOverTestSuiteList(const std::vector<TestSuite*>& case_list,
449 int (TestSuite::*method)() const) {
450 int sum = 0;
451 for (size_t i = 0; i < case_list.size(); i++) {
452 sum += (case_list[i]->*method)();
453 }
454 return sum;
455}

457// Returns true if and only if the test suite passed.
458static bool TestSuitePassed(const TestSuite* test_suite) {
459 return test_suite->should_run() && test_suite->Passed();
460}
461
462// Returns true if and only if the test suite failed.
463static bool TestSuiteFailed(const TestSuite* test_suite) {
464 return test_suite->should_run() && test_suite->Failed();
465}
466
467// Returns true if and only if test_suite contains at least one test that
468// should run.
469static bool ShouldRunTestSuite(const TestSuite* test_suite) {
470 return test_suite->should_run();
471}

475// Returns true if test part results of type `type` should include a stack
476// trace.
477bool ShouldEmitStackTraceForResultType(TestPartResult::Type type) {
478 // Suppress emission of the stack trace for SUCCEED() since it likely never
479 // requires investigation, and GTEST_SKIP() since skipping is an intentional
480 // act by the developer rather than a failure requiring investigation.
481 return type != TestPartResult::kSuccess && type != TestPartResult::kSkip;
482}

487AssertHelper::AssertHelper(TestPartResult::Type type, const char* file,
488 int line, const char* message)

490 type, file == nullptr ? std::string_view() : std::string_view(file),

493}
494
495AssertHelper::AssertHelper(TestPartResult::Type type,
496 const std::string_view file, int line,
497 const std::string_view message)
498 : data_(new AssertHelperData(type, file, line, message)) {}
499
500AssertHelper::~AssertHelper() { delete data_; }
501
502// Message assignment, for assertion streaming support.
503void AssertHelper::operator=(const Message& message) const {
504 UnitTest::GetInstance()->AddTestPartResult(
505 data_->type, data_->file, data_->line,
506 AppendUserMessage(data_->message, message),
507 ShouldEmitStackTraceForResultType(data_->type)
508 ? UnitTest::GetInstance()->impl()->CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(1)
509 : ""
510 // Skips the stack frame for this function itself.
511 ); // NOLINT
512}

516// When TEST_P is found without a matching INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P
517// to creates test cases for it, a synthetic test case is
518// inserted to report ether an error or a log message.
519//
520// This configuration bit will likely be removed at some point.
521constexpr bool kErrorOnUninstantiatedParameterizedTest = true;
522constexpr bool kErrorOnUninstantiatedTypeParameterizedTest = true;
523
524// A test that fails at a given file/line location with a given message.
525class FailureTest : public Test {
526 public:
527 explicit FailureTest(const CodeLocation& loc, std::string error_message,
528 bool as_error)
529 : loc_(loc),
530 error_message_(std::move(error_message)),
531 as_error_(as_error) {}
532
533 void TestBody() override {
534 if (as_error_) {
535 AssertHelper(TestPartResult::kNonFatalFailure, loc_.file.c_str(),
536 loc_.line, "") = Message() << error_message_;
537 } else {
538 std::cout << error_message_ << std::endl;
539 }
540 }
541
542 private:
543 const CodeLocation loc_;
544 const std::string error_message_;
545 const bool as_error_;
546};

559// If this parameterized test suite has no instantiations (and that
560// has not been marked as okay), emit a test case reporting that.
561void InsertSyntheticTestCase(const std::string& name, CodeLocation location,
562 bool has_test_p) {
563 const auto& ignored = *GetIgnoredParameterizedTestSuites();
564 if (ignored.find(name) != ignored.end()) return;
565
566 const char kMissingInstantiation[] = //
567 " is defined via TEST_P, but never instantiated. None of the test "
568 "cases "
569 "will run. Either no INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P is provided or the only "
570 "ones provided expand to nothing."
571 "\n\n"
572 "Ideally, TEST_P definitions should only ever be included as part of "
573 "binaries that intend to use them. (As opposed to, for example, being "
574 "placed in a library that may be linked in to get other utilities.)";
575
576 const char kMissingTestCase[] = //
577 " is instantiated via INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P, but no tests are "
578 "defined via TEST_P . No test cases will run."
579 "\n\n"
580 "Ideally, INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P should only ever be invoked from "
581 "code that always depend on code that provides TEST_P. Failing to do "
582 "so is often an indication of dead code, e.g. the last TEST_P was "
583 "removed but the rest got left behind.";
584
585 std::string message =
586 "Parameterized test suite " + name +
587 (has_test_p ? kMissingInstantiation : kMissingTestCase) +
588 "\n\n"
589 "To suppress this error for this test suite, insert the following line "
590 "(in a non-header) in the namespace it is defined in:"
591 "\n\n"
592 "GTEST_ALLOW_UNINSTANTIATED_PARAMETERIZED_TEST(" +
593 name + ");";
594
595 std::string full_name = "UninstantiatedParameterizedTestSuite<" + name + ">";
596 RegisterTest( //
597 "GoogleTestVerification", full_name.c_str(),
598 nullptr, // No type parameter.
599 nullptr, // No value parameter.
600 location.file.c_str(), location.line, [message, location] {
601 return new FailureTest(location, message,
602 kErrorOnUninstantiatedParameterizedTest);
603 });
604}

617void TypeParameterizedTestSuiteRegistry::RegisterTestSuite(
618 const char* test_suite_name, CodeLocation code_location) {
619 suites_.emplace(std::string(test_suite_name),
620 TypeParameterizedTestSuiteInfo(std::move(code_location)));
621}
622
623void TypeParameterizedTestSuiteRegistry::RegisterInstantiation(
624 const char* test_suite_name) {
625 auto it = suites_.find(std::string(test_suite_name));
626 if (it != suites_.end()) {
627 it->second.instantiated = true;
628 } else {
629 GTEST_LOG_(ERROR) << "Unknown type parameterized test suit '"
630 << test_suite_name << "'";
631 }
632}
633
634void TypeParameterizedTestSuiteRegistry::CheckForInstantiations() {
635 const auto& ignored = *GetIgnoredParameterizedTestSuites();
636 for (const auto& testcase : suites_) {
637 if (testcase.second.instantiated) continue;
638 if (ignored.find(testcase.first) != ignored.end()) continue;
639
640 std::string message =
641 "Type parameterized test suite " + testcase.first +
642 " is defined via REGISTER_TYPED_TEST_SUITE_P, but never instantiated "
643 "via INSTANTIATE_TYPED_TEST_SUITE_P. None of the test cases will run."
644 "\n\n"
645 "Ideally, TYPED_TEST_P definitions should only ever be included as "
646 "part of binaries that intend to use them. (As opposed to, for "
647 "example, being placed in a library that may be linked in to get "
648 "other "
649 "utilities.)"
650 "\n\n"
651 "To suppress this error for this test suite, insert the following "
652 "line "
653 "(in a non-header) in the namespace it is defined in:"
654 "\n\n"
655 "GTEST_ALLOW_UNINSTANTIATED_PARAMETERIZED_TEST(" +
656 testcase.first + ");";
657
658 std::string full_name =
659 "UninstantiatedTypeParameterizedTestSuite<" + testcase.first + ">";
660 RegisterTest( //
661 "GoogleTestVerification", full_name.c_str(),
662 nullptr, // No type parameter.
663 nullptr, // No value parameter.
664 testcase.second.code_location.file.c_str(),
665 testcase.second.code_location.line, [message, testcase] {
666 return new FailureTest(testcase.second.code_location, message,
667 kErrorOnUninstantiatedTypeParameterizedTest);
668 });
669 }
670}

708std::string UnitTestOptions::GetOutputFormat() {
709 std::string s = GTEST_FLAG_GET(output);
710 const char* const gtest_output_flag = s.c_str();
711 const char* const colon = strchr(gtest_output_flag, ':');

718#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
719// Returns the name of the requested output file, or the default if none
720// was explicitly specified.
721std::string UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile() {
722 std::string s = GTEST_FLAG_GET(output);
723 const char* const gtest_output_flag = s.c_str();
724
725 std::string format = GetOutputFormat();
726 if (format.empty()) format = kDefaultOutputFormat;
727
728 const char* const colon = strchr(gtest_output_flag, ':');
729 if (colon == nullptr)
730 return internal::FilePath::MakeFileName(
731 internal::FilePath(
732 UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir()),
733 internal::FilePath(kDefaultOutputFile), 0, format.c_str())
734 .string();
735
736 internal::FilePath output_name(colon + 1);
737 if (!output_name.IsAbsolutePath())
738 output_name = internal::FilePath::ConcatPaths(
739 internal::FilePath(UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir()),
740 internal::FilePath(colon + 1));
741
742 if (!output_name.IsDirectory()) return output_name.string();
743
744 internal::FilePath result(internal::FilePath::GenerateUniqueFileName(
745 output_name, internal::GetCurrentExecutableName(),
746 GetOutputFormat().c_str()));
747 return result.string();
748}

751// Returns true if and only if the wildcard pattern matches the string. Each
752// pattern consists of regular characters, single-character wildcards (?), and
753// multi-character wildcards (*).
754//
755// This function implements a linear-time string globbing algorithm based on
756// https://research.swtch.com/glob.
757static bool PatternMatchesString(const std::string& name_str,
758 const char* pattern, const char* pattern_end) {
759 const char* name = name_str.c_str();
760 const char* const name_begin = name;
761 const char* const name_end = name + name_str.size();
762
763 const char* pattern_next = pattern;
764 const char* name_next = name;
765
766 while (pattern < pattern_end || name < name_end) {
767 if (pattern < pattern_end) {
768 switch (*pattern) {
769 default: // Match an ordinary character.
770 if (name < name_end && *name == *pattern) {
771 ++pattern;
772 ++name;
773 continue;
774 }
775 break;
776 case '?': // Match any single character.
777 if (name < name_end) {
778 ++pattern;
779 ++name;
780 continue;
781 }
782 break;
783 case '*':
784 // Match zero or more characters. Start by skipping over the wildcard
785 // and matching zero characters from name. If that fails, restart and
786 // match one more character than the last attempt.
787 pattern_next = pattern;
788 name_next = name + 1;
789 ++pattern;
790 continue;
791 }
792 }
793 // Failed to match a character. Restart if possible.
794 if (name_begin < name_next && name_next <= name_end) {
795 pattern = pattern_next;
796 name = name_next;
797 continue;
798 }
799 return false;
800 }
801 return true;
802}
803
804namespace {
805
806bool IsGlobPattern(const std::string& pattern) {
807 return std::any_of(pattern.begin(), pattern.end(),
808 [](const char c) { return c == '?' || c == '*'; });
809}
810
811class UnitTestFilter {
812 public:
813 UnitTestFilter() = default;
814
815 // Constructs a filter from a string of patterns separated by `:`.
816 explicit UnitTestFilter(const std::string& filter) {
817 // By design "" filter matches "" string.
818 std::vector<std::string> all_patterns;
819 SplitString(filter, ':', &all_patterns);
820 const auto exact_match_patterns_begin = std::partition(
821 all_patterns.begin(), all_patterns.end(), &IsGlobPattern);
822
823 glob_patterns_.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(
824 std::distance(all_patterns.begin(), exact_match_patterns_begin)));
825 std::move(all_patterns.begin(), exact_match_patterns_begin,
826 std::inserter(glob_patterns_, glob_patterns_.begin()));
827 std::move(
828 exact_match_patterns_begin, all_patterns.end(),
829 std::inserter(exact_match_patterns_, exact_match_patterns_.begin()));
830 }
831
832 // Returns true if and only if name matches at least one of the patterns in
833 // the filter.
834 bool MatchesName(const std::string& name) const {
835 return exact_match_patterns_.find(name) != exact_match_patterns_.end() ||
836 std::any_of(glob_patterns_.begin(), glob_patterns_.end(),
837 [&name](const std::string& pattern) {
838 return PatternMatchesString(
839 name, pattern.c_str(),
840 pattern.c_str() + pattern.size());
841 });
842 }
843
844 private:
845 std::vector<std::string> glob_patterns_;
846 std::unordered_set<std::string> exact_match_patterns_;
847};
848
849class PositiveAndNegativeUnitTestFilter {
850 public:
851 // Constructs a positive and a negative filter from a string. The string
852 // contains a positive filter optionally followed by a '-' character and a
853 // negative filter. In case only a negative filter is provided the positive
854 // filter will be assumed "*".
855 // A filter is a list of patterns separated by ':'.
856 explicit PositiveAndNegativeUnitTestFilter(const std::string& filter) {
857 std::vector<std::string> positive_and_negative_filters;
858
859 // NOTE: `SplitString` always returns a non-empty container.
860 SplitString(filter, '-', &positive_and_negative_filters);
861 const auto& positive_filter = positive_and_negative_filters.front();
862
863 if (positive_and_negative_filters.size() > 1) {
864 positive_filter_ = UnitTestFilter(
865 positive_filter.empty() ? kUniversalFilter : positive_filter);
866
867 // TODO(b/214626361): Fail on multiple '-' characters
868 // For the moment to preserve old behavior we concatenate the rest of the
869 // string parts with `-` as separator to generate the negative filter.
870 auto negative_filter_string = positive_and_negative_filters[1];
871 for (std::size_t i = 2; i < positive_and_negative_filters.size(); i++)
872 negative_filter_string =
873 negative_filter_string + '-' + positive_and_negative_filters[i];
874 negative_filter_ = UnitTestFilter(negative_filter_string);
875 } else {
876 // In case we don't have a negative filter and positive filter is ""
877 // we do not use kUniversalFilter by design as opposed to when we have a
878 // negative filter.
879 positive_filter_ = UnitTestFilter(positive_filter);
880 }
881 }
882
883 // Returns true if and only if test name (this is generated by appending test
884 // suit name and test name via a '.' character) matches the positive filter
885 // and does not match the negative filter.
886 bool MatchesTest(const std::string& test_suite_name,
887 const std::string& test_name) const {
888 return MatchesName(test_suite_name + "." + test_name);
889 }
890
891 // Returns true if and only if name matches the positive filter and does not
892 // match the negative filter.
893 bool MatchesName(const std::string& name) const {
894 return positive_filter_.MatchesName(name) &&
895 !negative_filter_.MatchesName(name);
896 }
897
898 private:
899 UnitTestFilter positive_filter_;
900 UnitTestFilter negative_filter_;
901};
902} // namespace

909// Returns true if and only if the user-specified filter matches the test

911bool UnitTestOptions::FilterMatchesTest(const std::string& test_suite_name,

920static std::string FormatSehExceptionMessage(DWORD exception_code,
921 const char* location) {
922 Message message;
923 message << "SEH exception with code 0x" << std::setbase(16) << exception_code
924 << std::setbase(10) << " thrown in " << location << ".";
925 return message.GetString();
926}
927
928int UnitTestOptions::GTestProcessSEH(DWORD seh_code, const char* location) {
929 // Google Test should handle a SEH exception if:
930 // 1. the user wants it to, AND
931 // 2. this is not a breakpoint exception or stack overflow, AND
932 // 3. this is not a C++ exception (VC++ implements them via SEH,
933 // apparently).
934 //
935 // SEH exception code for C++ exceptions.
936 // (see https://support.microsoft.com/kb/185294 for more information).
937 const DWORD kCxxExceptionCode = 0xe06d7363;
938
939 if (!GTEST_FLAG_GET(catch_exceptions) || seh_code == kCxxExceptionCode ||
940 seh_code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT ||
941 seh_code == EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW) {
942 return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH; // Don't handle these exceptions
943 }
944
945 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(
946 TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
947 FormatSehExceptionMessage(seh_code, location) +
948 "\n"
949 "Stack trace:\n" +
950 ::testing::internal::GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(1));
951
952 return EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER;
953}
954#endif // GTEST_HAS_SEH

1022// This predicate-formatter checks that 'results' contains a test part
1023// failure of the given type and that the failure message contains the
1024// given substring.
1025static AssertionResult HasOneFailure(const char* /* results_expr */,
1026 const char* /* type_expr */,
1027 const char* /* substr_expr */,
1028 const TestPartResultArray& results,
1029 TestPartResult::Type type,
1030 const std::string& substr) {
1031 const std::string expected(type == TestPartResult::kFatalFailure
1032 ? "1 fatal failure"
1033 : "1 non-fatal failure");
1034 Message msg;
1035 if (results.size() != 1) {
1036 msg << "Expected: " << expected << "\n"
1037 << " Actual: " << results.size() << " failures";
1038 for (int i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
1039 msg << "\n" << results.GetTestPartResult(i);
1040 }
1041 return AssertionFailure() << msg;
1042 }
1043
1044 const TestPartResult& r = results.GetTestPartResult(0);
1045 if (r.type() != type) {
1046 return AssertionFailure() << "Expected: " << expected << "\n"
1047 << " Actual:\n"
1048 << r;
1049 }
1050
1051 if (strstr(r.message(), substr.c_str()) == nullptr) {
1052 return AssertionFailure()
1053 << "Expected: " << expected << " containing \"" << substr << "\"\n"
1054 << " Actual:\n"
1055 << r;
1056 }
1057
1058 return AssertionSuccess();
1059}

1061// The constructor of SingleFailureChecker remembers where to look up
1062// test part results, what type of failure we expect, and what
1063// substring the failure message should contain.
1064SingleFailureChecker::SingleFailureChecker(const TestPartResultArray* results,
1065 TestPartResult::Type type,

1071// type and contains the given substring. If that's not the case, a
1072// non-fatal failure will be generated.
1073SingleFailureChecker::~SingleFailureChecker() {
1074 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT3(HasOneFailure, *results_, type_, substr_);
1075}

1202// A helper class for measuring elapsed times.
1203class Timer {
1204 public:
1205 Timer() : start_(clock::now()) {}
1206
1207 // Return time elapsed in milliseconds since the timer was created.
1208 TimeInMillis Elapsed() {
1209 return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(clock::now() -
1210 start_)
1211 .count();
1212 }
1213
1214 private:
1215 // Fall back to the system_clock when building with newlib on a system
1216 // without a monotonic clock.
1217#if defined(_NEWLIB_VERSION) && !defined(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
1218 using clock = std::chrono::system_clock;
1219#else
1220 using clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
1221#endif
1222 clock::time_point start_;
1223};
1224
1225// Returns a timestamp as milliseconds since the epoch. Note this time may jump
1226// around subject to adjustments by the system, to measure elapsed time use
1227// Timer instead.
1228TimeInMillis GetTimeInMillis() {
1229 return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
1230 std::chrono::system_clock::now() -
1231 std::chrono::system_clock::from_time_t(0))
1232 .count();
1233}

1239#ifdef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
1240// Creates a UTF-16 wide string from the given ANSI string, allocating
1241// memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
1242// value using delete[]. Returns the wide string, or NULL if the
1243// input is NULL.
1244LPCWSTR String::AnsiToUtf16(const char* ansi) {
1245 if (!ansi) return nullptr;
1246 const int length = strlen(ansi);
1247 const int unicode_length =
1248 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, ansi, length, nullptr, 0);
1249 WCHAR* unicode = new WCHAR[unicode_length + 1];
1250 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, ansi, length, unicode, unicode_length);
1251 unicode[unicode_length] = 0;
1252 return unicode;
1253}
1254
1255// Creates an ANSI string from the given wide string, allocating
1256// memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
1257// value using delete[]. Returns the ANSI string, or NULL if the
1258// input is NULL.
1259const char* String::Utf16ToAnsi(LPCWSTR utf16_str) {
1260 if (!utf16_str) return nullptr;
1261 const int ansi_length = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, utf16_str, -1, nullptr,
1262 0, nullptr, nullptr);
1263 char* ansi = new char[ansi_length + 1];
1264 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, utf16_str, -1, ansi, ansi_length, nullptr,
1265 nullptr);
1266 ansi[ansi_length] = 0;
1267 return ansi;
1268}
1269
1270#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
1271
1272// Compares two C strings. Returns true if and only if they have the same
1273// content.
1274//
1275// Unlike strcmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A NULL
1276// C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
1277// including the empty string.
1278bool String::CStringEquals(const char* lhs, const char* rhs) {
1279 if (lhs == nullptr) return rhs == nullptr;
1280
1281 if (rhs == nullptr) return false;
1282
1283 return strcmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
1284}
1285
1286#if GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
1287
1288// Converts an array of wide chars to a narrow string using the UTF-8
1289// encoding, and streams the result to the given Message object.
1290static void StreamWideCharsToMessage(const wchar_t* wstr, size_t length,
1291 Message* msg) {
1292 for (size_t i = 0; i != length;) { // NOLINT
1293 if (wstr[i] != L'\0') {
1294 *msg << WideStringToUtf8(wstr + i, static_cast<int>(length - i));
1295 while (i != length && wstr[i] != L'\0') i++;
1296 } else {
1297 *msg << '\0';
1298 i++;
1299 }
1300 }
1301}

1303#endif // GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
1304
1305void SplitString(const ::std::string& str, char delimiter,
1306 ::std::vector< ::std::string>* dest) {
1307 ::std::vector< ::std::string> parsed;
1308 ::std::string::size_type pos = 0;
1309 while (::testing::internal::AlwaysTrue()) {
1310 const ::std::string::size_type colon = str.find(delimiter, pos);
1311 if (colon == ::std::string::npos) {
1312 parsed.push_back(str.substr(pos));
1313 break;
1314 } else {
1315 parsed.push_back(str.substr(pos, colon - pos));
1316 pos = colon + 1;
1317 }
1318 }
1319 dest->swap(parsed);
1320}

1324// Constructs an empty Message.
1325// We allocate the stringstream separately because otherwise each use of
1326// ASSERT/EXPECT in a procedure adds over 200 bytes to the procedure's
1327// stack frame leading to huge stack frames in some cases; gcc does not reuse
1328// the stack space.
1329Message::Message() : ss_(new ::std::stringstream) {
1330 // By default, we want there to be enough precision when printing
1331 // a double to a Message.
1332 *ss_ << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<double>::digits10 + 2);
1333}

1335// These two overloads allow streaming a wide C string to a Message
1336// using the UTF-8 encoding.
1337Message& Message::operator<<(const wchar_t* wide_c_str) {
1338 return *this << internal::String::ShowWideCString(wide_c_str);
1339}
1340Message& Message::operator<<(wchar_t* wide_c_str) {
1341 return *this << internal::String::ShowWideCString(wide_c_str);
1342}

1344#if GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
1345// Converts the given wide string to a narrow string using the UTF-8
1346// encoding, and streams the result to this Message object.
1347Message& Message::operator<<(const ::std::wstring& wstr) {
1348 internal::StreamWideCharsToMessage(wstr.c_str(), wstr.length(), this);
1349 return *this;
1350}

1361namespace edit_distance {
1362std::vector<EditType> CalculateOptimalEdits(const std::vector<size_t>& left,
1363 const std::vector<size_t>& right) {
1364 std::vector<std::vector<double> > costs(
1365 left.size() + 1, std::vector<double>(right.size() + 1));
1366 std::vector<std::vector<EditType> > best_move(
1367 left.size() + 1, std::vector<EditType>(right.size() + 1));
1368
1369 // Populate for empty right.
1370 for (size_t l_i = 0; l_i < costs.size(); ++l_i) {
1371 costs[l_i][0] = static_cast<double>(l_i);
1372 best_move[l_i][0] = kRemove;
1373 }
1374 // Populate for empty left.
1375 for (size_t r_i = 1; r_i < costs[0].size(); ++r_i) {
1376 costs[0][r_i] = static_cast<double>(r_i);
1377 best_move[0][r_i] = kAdd;
1378 }
1379
1380 for (size_t l_i = 0; l_i < left.size(); ++l_i) {
1381 for (size_t r_i = 0; r_i < right.size(); ++r_i) {
1382 if (left[l_i] == right[r_i]) {
1383 // Found a match. Consume it.
1384 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = costs[l_i][r_i];
1385 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kMatch;
1386 continue;
1387 }
1388
1389 const double add = costs[l_i + 1][r_i];
1390 const double remove = costs[l_i][r_i + 1];
1391 const double replace = costs[l_i][r_i];
1392 if (add < remove && add < replace) {
1393 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = add + 1;
1394 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kAdd;
1395 } else if (remove < add && remove < replace) {
1396 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = remove + 1;
1397 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kRemove;
1398 } else {
1399 // We make replace a little more expensive than add/remove to lower
1400 // their priority.
1401 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = replace + 1.00001;
1402 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kReplace;
1403 }
1404 }
1405 }
1406
1407 // Reconstruct the best path. We do it in reverse order.
1408 std::vector<EditType> best_path;
1409 for (size_t l_i = left.size(), r_i = right.size(); l_i > 0 || r_i > 0;) {
1410 EditType move = best_move[l_i][r_i];
1411 best_path.push_back(move);
1412 l_i -= move != kAdd;
1413 r_i -= move != kRemove;
1414 }
1415 std::reverse(best_path.begin(), best_path.end());
1416 return best_path;
1417}

1421// Helper class to convert string into ids with deduplication.
1422class InternalStrings {
1423 public:
1424 size_t GetId(const std::string& str) {
1425 IdMap::iterator it = ids_.find(str);
1426 if (it != ids_.end()) return it->second;
1427 size_t id = ids_.size();
1428 return ids_[str] = id;

1437
1438std::vector<EditType> CalculateOptimalEdits(
1439 const std::vector<std::string>& left,
1440 const std::vector<std::string>& right) {
1441 std::vector<size_t> left_ids, right_ids;
1442 {
1443 InternalStrings intern_table;
1444 for (size_t i = 0; i < left.size(); ++i) {
1445 left_ids.push_back(intern_table.GetId(left[i]));
1446 }
1447 for (size_t i = 0; i < right.size(); ++i) {
1448 right_ids.push_back(intern_table.GetId(right[i]));
1449 }
1450 }
1451 return CalculateOptimalEdits(left_ids, right_ids);
1452}

1454namespace {
1455
1456// Helper class that holds the state for one hunk and prints it out to the
1457// stream.
1458// It reorders adds/removes when possible to group all removes before all
1459// adds. It also adds the hunk header before printint into the stream.
1460class Hunk {
1461 public:
1462 Hunk(size_t left_start, size_t right_start)
1463 : left_start_(left_start),
1464 right_start_(right_start),
1465 adds_(),
1466 removes_(),
1467 common_() {}
1468
1469 void PushLine(char edit, const char* line) {
1470 switch (edit) {
1471 case ' ':
1472 ++common_;
1473 FlushEdits();
1474 hunk_.push_back(std::make_pair(' ', line));
1475 break;
1476 case '-':
1477 ++removes_;
1478 hunk_removes_.push_back(std::make_pair('-', line));
1479 break;
1480 case '+':
1481 ++adds_;
1482 hunk_adds_.push_back(std::make_pair('+', line));
1483 break;
1484 }
1485 }
1486
1487 void PrintTo(std::ostream* os) {
1488 PrintHeader(os);
1489 FlushEdits();
1490 for (std::list<std::pair<char, const char*> >::const_iterator it =
1491 hunk_.begin();
1492 it != hunk_.end(); ++it) {
1493 *os << it->first << it->second << "\n";
1494 }
1495 }
1496
1497 bool has_edits() const { return adds_ || removes_; }
1498
1499 private:
1500 void FlushEdits() {
1501 hunk_.splice(hunk_.end(), hunk_removes_);
1502 hunk_.splice(hunk_.end(), hunk_adds_);
1503 }
1504
1505 // Print a unified diff header for one hunk.
1506 // The format is
1507 // "@@ -<left_start>,<left_length> +<right_start>,<right_length> @@"
1508 // where the left/right lengths are omitted if unnecessary.
1509 void PrintHeader(std::ostream* ss) const {
1510 size_t left_length = removes_ + common_;
1511 size_t right_length = adds_ + common_;
1512 *ss << "@@ " << "-" << left_start_;
1513 if (left_length != 1) {
1514 *ss << "," << left_length;
1515 }
1516 *ss << " " << "+" << right_start_;
1517 if (right_length != 1) {
1518 *ss << "," << right_length;
1519 }
1520 *ss << " @@\n";
1521 }
1522
1523 size_t left_start_, right_start_;
1524 size_t adds_, removes_, common_;
1525 std::list<std::pair<char, const char*> > hunk_, hunk_adds_, hunk_removes_;
1526};
1527
1528} // namespace
1529
1530// Create a list of diff hunks in Unified diff format.
1531// Each hunk has a header generated by PrintHeader above plus a body with
1532// lines prefixed with ' ' for no change, '-' for deletion and '+' for
1533// addition.
1534// 'context' represents the desired unchanged prefix/suffix around the diff.
1535// If two hunks are close enough that their contexts overlap, then they are
1536// joined into one hunk.
1537std::string CreateUnifiedDiff(const std::vector<std::string>& left,
1538 const std::vector<std::string>& right,
1539 size_t context) {
1540 const std::vector<EditType> edits = CalculateOptimalEdits(left, right);
1541
1542 size_t l_i = 0, r_i = 0, edit_i = 0;
1543 std::stringstream ss;
1544 while (edit_i < edits.size()) {
1545 // Find first edit.
1546 while (edit_i < edits.size() && edits[edit_i] == kMatch) {
1547 ++l_i;
1548 ++r_i;
1549 ++edit_i;
1550 }
1551
1552 // Find the first line to include in the hunk.
1553 const size_t prefix_context = std::min(l_i, context);
1554 Hunk hunk(l_i - prefix_context + 1, r_i - prefix_context + 1);
1555 for (size_t i = prefix_context; i > 0; --i) {
1556 hunk.PushLine(' ', left[l_i - i].c_str());
1557 }
1558
1559 // Iterate the edits until we found enough suffix for the hunk or the input
1560 // is over.
1561 size_t n_suffix = 0;
1562 for (; edit_i < edits.size(); ++edit_i) {
1563 if (n_suffix >= context) {
1564 // Continue only if the next hunk is very close.
1565 auto it = edits.begin() + static_cast<int>(edit_i);
1566 while (it != edits.end() && *it == kMatch) ++it;
1567 if (it == edits.end() ||
1568 static_cast<size_t>(it - edits.begin()) - edit_i >= context) {
1569 // There is no next edit or it is too far away.
1570 break;
1571 }
1572 }
1573
1574 EditType edit = edits[edit_i];
1575 // Reset count when a non match is found.
1576 n_suffix = edit == kMatch ? n_suffix + 1 : 0;
1577
1578 if (edit == kMatch || edit == kRemove || edit == kReplace) {
1579 hunk.PushLine(edit == kMatch ? ' ' : '-', left[l_i].c_str());
1580 }
1581 if (edit == kAdd || edit == kReplace) {
1582 hunk.PushLine('+', right[r_i].c_str());
1583 }
1584
1585 // Advance indices, depending on edit type.
1586 l_i += edit != kAdd;
1587 r_i += edit != kRemove;
1588 }
1589
1590 if (!hunk.has_edits()) {
1591 // We are done. We don't want this hunk.
1592 break;
1593 }
1594
1595 hunk.PrintTo(&ss);
1596 }
1597 return ss.str();
1598}

1604// The string representation of the values received in EqFailure() are already
1605// escaped. Split them on escaped '\n' boundaries. Leave all other escaped
1606// characters the same.
1607std::vector<std::string> SplitEscapedString(const std::string& str) {
1608 std::vector<std::string> lines;
1609 size_t start = 0, end = str.size();
1610 if (end > 2 && str[0] == '"' && str[end - 1] == '"') {
1611 ++start;
1612 --end;
1613 }
1614 bool escaped = false;
1615 for (size_t i = start; i + 1 < end; ++i) {
1616 if (escaped) {
1617 escaped = false;
1618 if (str[i] == 'n') {
1619 lines.push_back(str.substr(start, i - start - 1));
1620 start = i + 1;
1621 }
1622 } else {
1623 escaped = str[i] == '\\';
1624 }
1625 }
1626 lines.push_back(str.substr(start, end - start));
1627 return lines;
1628}

1632// Constructs and returns the message for an equality assertion
1633// (e.g. ASSERT_EQ, EXPECT_STREQ, etc) failure.
1634//
1635// The first four parameters are the expressions used in the assertion
1636// and their values, as strings. For example, for ASSERT_EQ(foo, bar)
1637// where foo is 5 and bar is 6, we have:
1638//
1639// lhs_expression: "foo"
1640// rhs_expression: "bar"
1641// lhs_value: "5"
1642// rhs_value: "6"
1643//
1644// The ignoring_case parameter is true if and only if the assertion is a
1645// *_STRCASEEQ*. When it's true, the string "Ignoring case" will
1646// be inserted into the message.
1647AssertionResult EqFailure(const char* lhs_expression,
1648 const char* rhs_expression,
1649 const std::string& lhs_value,
1650 const std::string& rhs_value, bool ignoring_case) {
1651 Message msg;
1652 msg << "Expected equality of these values:";
1653 msg << "\n " << lhs_expression;
1654 if (lhs_value != lhs_expression) {
1655 msg << "\n Which is: " << lhs_value;
1656 }
1657 msg << "\n " << rhs_expression;
1658 if (rhs_value != rhs_expression) {
1659 msg << "\n Which is: " << rhs_value;
1660 }
1661
1662 if (ignoring_case) {
1663 msg << "\nIgnoring case";
1664 }
1665
1666 if (!lhs_value.empty() && !rhs_value.empty()) {
1667 const std::vector<std::string> lhs_lines = SplitEscapedString(lhs_value);
1668 const std::vector<std::string> rhs_lines = SplitEscapedString(rhs_value);
1669 if (lhs_lines.size() > 1 || rhs_lines.size() > 1) {
1670 msg << "\nWith diff:\n"
1671 << edit_distance::CreateUnifiedDiff(lhs_lines, rhs_lines);
1672 }
1673 }
1674
1675 return AssertionFailure() << msg;
1676}

1678// Constructs a failure message for Boolean assertions such as EXPECT_TRUE.
1679std::string GetBoolAssertionFailureMessage(
1680 const AssertionResult& assertion_result, const char* expression_text,
1681 const char* actual_predicate_value, const char* expected_predicate_value) {
1682 const char* actual_message = assertion_result.message();
1683 Message msg;
1684 msg << "Value of: " << expression_text
1685 << "\n Actual: " << actual_predicate_value;
1686 if (actual_message[0] != '\0') msg << " (" << actual_message << ")";
1687 msg << "\nExpected: " << expected_predicate_value;
1688 return msg.GetString();
1689}

1691// Helper function for implementing ASSERT_NEAR. Treats infinity as a specific
1692// value, such that comparing infinity to infinity is equal, the distance
1693// between -infinity and +infinity is infinity, and infinity <= infinity is
1694// true.
1695AssertionResult DoubleNearPredFormat(const char* expr1, const char* expr2,
1696 const char* abs_error_expr, double val1,
1697 double val2, double abs_error) {
1698 // We want to return success when the two values are infinity and at least
1699 // one of the following is true:
1700 // * The values are the same-signed infinity.
1701 // * The error limit itself is infinity.
1702 // This is done here so that we don't end up with a NaN when calculating the
1703 // difference in values.
1704 if (std::isinf(val1) && std::isinf(val2) &&
1705 (std::signbit(val1) == std::signbit(val2) ||
1706 (abs_error > 0.0 && std::isinf(abs_error)))) {
1707 return AssertionSuccess();
1708 }
1709
1710 const double diff = fabs(val1 - val2);
1711 if (diff <= abs_error) return AssertionSuccess();
1712
1713 // Find the value which is closest to zero.
1714 const double min_abs = std::min(fabs(val1), fabs(val2));
1715 // Find the distance to the next double from that value.
1716 const double epsilon =
1717 nextafter(min_abs, std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()) - min_abs;
1718 // Detect the case where abs_error is so small that EXPECT_NEAR is
1719 // effectively the same as EXPECT_EQUAL, and give an informative error
1720 // message so that the situation can be more easily understood without
1721 // requiring exotic floating-point knowledge.
1722 // Don't do an epsilon check if abs_error is zero because that implies
1723 // that an equality check was actually intended.
1724 if (!(std::isnan)(val1) && !(std::isnan)(val2) && abs_error > 0 &&
1725 abs_error < epsilon) {
1726 return AssertionFailure()
1727 << "The difference between " << expr1 << " and " << expr2 << " is "
1728 << diff << ", where\n"
1729 << expr1 << " evaluates to " << val1 << ",\n"
1730 << expr2 << " evaluates to " << val2 << ".\nThe abs_error parameter "
1731 << abs_error_expr << " evaluates to " << abs_error
1732 << " which is smaller than the minimum distance between doubles for "
1733 "numbers of this magnitude which is "
1734 << epsilon
1735 << ", thus making this EXPECT_NEAR check equivalent to "
1736 "EXPECT_EQUAL. Consider using EXPECT_DOUBLE_EQ instead.";
1737 }
1738 return AssertionFailure()
1739 << "The difference between " << expr1 << " and " << expr2 << " is "
1740 << diff << ", which exceeds " << abs_error_expr << ", where\n"
1741 << expr1 << " evaluates to " << val1 << ",\n"
1742 << expr2 << " evaluates to " << val2 << ", and\n"
1743 << abs_error_expr << " evaluates to " << abs_error << ".";
1744}
1745
1746// Helper template for implementing FloatLE() and DoubleLE().
1747template <typename RawType>
1748AssertionResult FloatingPointLE(const char* expr1, const char* expr2,
1749 RawType val1, RawType val2) {
1750 // Returns success if val1 is less than val2,
1751 if (val1 < val2) {
1752 return AssertionSuccess();
1753 }
1754
1755 // or if val1 is almost equal to val2.
1756 const FloatingPoint<RawType> lhs(val1), rhs(val2);
1757 if (lhs.AlmostEquals(rhs)) {
1758 return AssertionSuccess();
1759 }
1760
1761 // Note that the above two checks will both fail if either val1 or
1762 // val2 is NaN, as the IEEE floating-point standard requires that
1763 // any predicate involving a NaN must return false.
1764
1765 ::std::stringstream val1_ss;
1766 val1_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
1767 << val1;
1768
1769 ::std::stringstream val2_ss;
1770 val2_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
1771 << val2;
1772
1773 return AssertionFailure()
1774 << "Expected: (" << expr1 << ") <= (" << expr2 << ")\n"
1775 << " Actual: " << StringStreamToString(&val1_ss) << " vs "
1776 << StringStreamToString(&val2_ss);
1777}

1781// Asserts that val1 is less than, or almost equal to, val2. Fails
1782// otherwise. In particular, it fails if either val1 or val2 is NaN.
1783AssertionResult FloatLE(const char* expr1, const char* expr2, float val1,
1784 float val2) {
1785 return internal::FloatingPointLE<float>(expr1, expr2, val1, val2);
1786}
1787
1788// Asserts that val1 is less than, or almost equal to, val2. Fails
1789// otherwise. In particular, it fails if either val1 or val2 is NaN.
1790AssertionResult DoubleLE(const char* expr1, const char* expr2, double val1,
1791 double val2) {
1792 return internal::FloatingPointLE<double>(expr1, expr2, val1, val2);
1793}

1812 const char* rhs) {
1813 if (String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(lhs, rhs)) {
1814 return AssertionSuccess();

1851// Helper functions for implementing IsSubString() and IsNotSubstring().
1852
1853// This group of overloaded functions return true if and only if needle
1854// is a substring of haystack. NULL is considered a substring of
1855// itself only.
1856
1857bool IsSubstringPred(const char* needle, const char* haystack) {
1858 if (needle == nullptr || haystack == nullptr) return needle == haystack;
1859
1860 return strstr(haystack, needle) != nullptr;
1861}
1862
1863bool IsSubstringPred(const wchar_t* needle, const wchar_t* haystack) {
1864 if (needle == nullptr || haystack == nullptr) return needle == haystack;
1865
1866 return wcsstr(haystack, needle) != nullptr;
1867}
1868
1869// StringType here can be either ::std::string or ::std::wstring.
1870template <typename StringType>
1871bool IsSubstringPred(const StringType& needle, const StringType& haystack) {
1872 return haystack.find(needle) != StringType::npos;
1873}
1874
1875// This function implements either IsSubstring() or IsNotSubstring(),
1876// depending on the value of the expected_to_be_substring parameter.
1877// StringType here can be const char*, const wchar_t*, ::std::string,
1878// or ::std::wstring.
1879template <typename StringType>
1880AssertionResult IsSubstringImpl(bool expected_to_be_substring,
1881 const char* needle_expr,
1882 const char* haystack_expr,
1883 const StringType& needle,
1884 const StringType& haystack) {
1885 if (IsSubstringPred(needle, haystack) == expected_to_be_substring)
1886 return AssertionSuccess();
1887
1888 const bool is_wide_string = sizeof(needle[0]) > 1;
1889 const char* const begin_string_quote = is_wide_string ? "L\"" : "\"";
1890 return AssertionFailure()
1891 << "Value of: " << needle_expr << "\n"
1892 << " Actual: " << begin_string_quote << needle << "\"\n"
1893 << "Expected: " << (expected_to_be_substring ? "" : "not ")
1894 << "a substring of " << haystack_expr << "\n"
1895 << "Which is: " << begin_string_quote << haystack << "\"";
1896}

1899
1900// IsSubstring() and IsNotSubstring() check whether needle is a
1901// substring of haystack (NULL is considered a substring of itself

1960// Helper function for IsHRESULT{SuccessFailure} predicates
1961AssertionResult HRESULTFailureHelper(const char* expr, const char* expected,
1962 long hr) { // NOLINT
1963#if defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE) || defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_TV_TITLE)
1964
1965 // Windows CE doesn't support FormatMessage.
1966 const char error_text[] = "";
1967
1968#else
1969
1970 // Looks up the human-readable system message for the HRESULT code
1971 // and since we're not passing any params to FormatMessage, we don't
1972 // want inserts expanded.
1973 const DWORD kFlags =
1974 FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM | FORMAT_MESSAGE_IGNORE_INSERTS;
1975 const DWORD kBufSize = 4096;
1976 // Gets the system's human readable message string for this HRESULT.
1977 char error_text[kBufSize] = {'\0'};
1978 DWORD message_length = ::FormatMessageA(kFlags,
1979 0, // no source, we're asking system
1980 static_cast<DWORD>(hr), // the error
1981 0, // no line width restrictions
1982 error_text, // output buffer
1983 kBufSize, // buf size
1984 nullptr); // no arguments for inserts
1985 // Trims tailing white space (FormatMessage leaves a trailing CR-LF)
1986 for (; message_length && IsSpace(error_text[message_length - 1]);
1987 --message_length) {
1988 error_text[message_length - 1] = '\0';
1989 }
1990
1991#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
1992
1993 const std::string error_hex("0x" + String::FormatHexInt(hr));
1994 return ::testing::AssertionFailure()
1995 << "Expected: " << expr << " " << expected << ".\n"
1996 << " Actual: " << error_hex << " " << error_text << "\n";
1997}
1998
1999} // namespace
2000
2001AssertionResult IsHRESULTSuccess(const char* expr, long hr) { // NOLINT
2002 if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
2003 return AssertionSuccess();
2004 }
2005 return HRESULTFailureHelper(expr, "succeeds", hr);
2006}
2007
2008AssertionResult IsHRESULTFailure(const char* expr, long hr) { // NOLINT
2009 if (FAILED(hr)) {
2010 return AssertionSuccess();
2011 }
2012 return HRESULTFailureHelper(expr, "fails", hr);
2013}

2017// Utility functions for encoding Unicode text (wide strings) in
2018// UTF-8.
2019
2020// A Unicode code-point can have up to 21 bits, and is encoded in UTF-8
2021// like this:
2022//
2023// Code-point length Encoding
2024// 0 - 7 bits 0xxxxxxx
2025// 8 - 11 bits 110xxxxx 10xxxxxx
2026// 12 - 16 bits 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
2027// 17 - 21 bits 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
2028
2029// The maximum code-point a one-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
2030constexpr uint32_t kMaxCodePoint1 = (static_cast<uint32_t>(1) << 7) - 1;
2031
2032// The maximum code-point a two-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
2033constexpr uint32_t kMaxCodePoint2 = (static_cast<uint32_t>(1) << (5 + 6)) - 1;
2034
2035// The maximum code-point a three-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
2036constexpr uint32_t kMaxCodePoint3 =
2037 (static_cast<uint32_t>(1) << (4 + 2 * 6)) - 1;
2038
2039// The maximum code-point a four-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
2040constexpr uint32_t kMaxCodePoint4 =
2041 (static_cast<uint32_t>(1) << (3 + 3 * 6)) - 1;
2042
2043// Chops off the n lowest bits from a bit pattern. Returns the n
2044// lowest bits. As a side effect, the original bit pattern will be
2045// shifted to the right by n bits.
2046inline uint32_t ChopLowBits(uint32_t* bits, int n) {
2047 const uint32_t low_bits = *bits & ((static_cast<uint32_t>(1) << n) - 1);
2048 *bits >>= n;
2049 return low_bits;
2050}
2051
2052// Converts a Unicode code point to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.
2053// code_point parameter is of type uint32_t because wchar_t may not be
2054// wide enough to contain a code point.
2055// If the code_point is not a valid Unicode code point
2056// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) it will be converted
2057// to "(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)".
2058std::string CodePointToUtf8(uint32_t code_point) {
2059 if (code_point > kMaxCodePoint4) {
2060 return "(Invalid Unicode 0x" + String::FormatHexUInt32(code_point) + ")";
2061 }
2062
2063 char str[5]; // Big enough for the largest valid code point.
2064 if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint1) {
2065 str[1] = '\0';
2066 str[0] = static_cast<char>(code_point); // 0xxxxxxx
2067 } else if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint2) {
2068 str[2] = '\0';
2069 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2070 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xC0 | code_point); // 110xxxxx
2071 } else if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint3) {
2072 str[3] = '\0';
2073 str[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2074 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2075 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xE0 | code_point); // 1110xxxx
2076 } else { // code_point <= kMaxCodePoint4
2077 str[4] = '\0';
2078 str[3] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2079 str[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2080 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
2081 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xF0 | code_point); // 11110xxx
2082 }
2083 return str;
2084}
2085
2086// The following two functions only make sense if the system
2087// uses UTF-16 for wide string encoding. All supported systems
2088// with 16 bit wchar_t (Windows, Cygwin) do use UTF-16.
2089
2090// Determines if the arguments constitute UTF-16 surrogate pair
2091// and thus should be combined into a single Unicode code point
2092// using CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair.
2093inline bool IsUtf16SurrogatePair(wchar_t first, wchar_t second) {
2094 return sizeof(wchar_t) == 2 && (first & 0xFC00) == 0xD800 &&
2095 (second & 0xFC00) == 0xDC00;
2096}
2097
2098// Creates a Unicode code point from UTF16 surrogate pair.
2099inline uint32_t CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair(wchar_t first,
2100 wchar_t second) {
2101 const auto first_u = static_cast<uint32_t>(first);
2102 const auto second_u = static_cast<uint32_t>(second);
2103 const uint32_t mask = (1 << 10) - 1;
2104 return (sizeof(wchar_t) == 2)
2105 ? (((first_u & mask) << 10) | (second_u & mask)) + 0x10000
2106 :
2107 // This function should not be called when the condition is
2108 // false, but we provide a sensible default in case it is.
2109 first_u;
2110}
2111
2112// Converts a wide string to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.
2113// The wide string is assumed to have the following encoding:
2114// UTF-16 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 2 (on Windows, Cygwin)
2115// UTF-32 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 4 (on Linux)
2116// Parameter str points to a null-terminated wide string.
2117// Parameter num_chars may additionally limit the number
2118// of wchar_t characters processed. -1 is used when the entire string
2119// should be processed.
2120// If the string contains code points that are not valid Unicode code points
2121// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) they will be output
2122// as '(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)'. If the string is in UTF16 encoding
2123// and contains invalid UTF-16 surrogate pairs, values in those pairs
2124// will be encoded as individual Unicode characters from Basic Normal Plane.
2125std::string WideStringToUtf8(const wchar_t* str, int num_chars) {
2126 if (num_chars == -1) num_chars = static_cast<int>(wcslen(str));
2127
2128 ::std::stringstream stream;
2129 for (int i = 0; i < num_chars; ++i) {
2130 uint32_t unicode_code_point;
2131
2132 if (str[i] == L'\0') {
2133 break;
2134 } else if (i + 1 < num_chars && IsUtf16SurrogatePair(str[i], str[i + 1])) {
2135 unicode_code_point =
2136 CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair(str[i], str[i + 1]);
2137 i++;
2138 } else {
2139 unicode_code_point = static_cast<uint32_t>(str[i]);
2140 }
2141
2142 stream << CodePointToUtf8(unicode_code_point);
2143 }
2144 return StringStreamToString(&stream);
2145}

2147// Converts a wide C string to an std::string using the UTF-8 encoding.
2148// NULL will be converted to "(null)".
2149std::string String::ShowWideCString(const wchar_t* wide_c_str) {
2150 if (wide_c_str == nullptr) return "(null)";
2151
2152 return internal::WideStringToUtf8(wide_c_str, -1);
2153}

2155// Compares two wide C strings. Returns true if and only if they have the
2156// same content.
2157//
2158// Unlike wcscmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A NULL
2159// C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
2160// including the empty string.
2161bool String::WideCStringEquals(const wchar_t* lhs, const wchar_t* rhs) {
2162 if (lhs == nullptr) return rhs == nullptr;
2163
2164 if (rhs == nullptr) return false;
2165
2166 return wcscmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
2167}

2170AssertionResult CmpHelperSTREQ(const char* lhs_expression,
2171 const char* rhs_expression, const wchar_t* lhs,
2172 const wchar_t* rhs) {
2173 if (String::WideCStringEquals(lhs, rhs)) {
2174 return AssertionSuccess();
2175 }
2176
2177 return EqFailure(lhs_expression, rhs_expression, PrintToString(lhs),
2178 PrintToString(rhs), false);

2182AssertionResult CmpHelperSTRNE(const char* s1_expression,
2183 const char* s2_expression, const wchar_t* s1,
2184 const wchar_t* s2) {
2185 if (!String::WideCStringEquals(s1, s2)) {
2186 return AssertionSuccess();

2190 << "Expected: (" << s1_expression << ") != (" << s2_expression
2191 << "), actual: " << PrintToString(s1) << " vs " << PrintToString(s2);
2192}

2194// Compares two C strings, ignoring case. Returns true if and only if they have
2195// the same content.
2196//
2197// Unlike strcasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A
2198// NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
2199// including the empty string.
2200bool String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(const char* lhs, const char* rhs) {
2201 if (lhs == nullptr) return rhs == nullptr;
2202 if (rhs == nullptr) return false;
2203 return posix::StrCaseCmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
2204}
2205
2206// Compares two wide C strings, ignoring case. Returns true if and only if they
2207// have the same content.
2208//
2209// Unlike wcscasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s).
2210// A NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL wide C string,
2211// including the empty string.
2212// NB: The implementations on different platforms slightly differ.
2213// On windows, this method uses _wcsicmp which compares according to LC_CTYPE
2214// environment variable. On GNU platform this method uses wcscasecmp
2215// which compares according to LC_CTYPE category of the current locale.
2216// On MacOS X, it uses towlower, which also uses LC_CTYPE category of the
2217// current locale.
2218bool String::CaseInsensitiveWideCStringEquals(const wchar_t* lhs,
2219 const wchar_t* rhs) {
2220 if (lhs == nullptr) return rhs == nullptr;
2221
2222 if (rhs == nullptr) return false;
2223
2224#ifdef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
2225 return _wcsicmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
2226#elif defined(GTEST_OS_LINUX) && !defined(GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID)
2227 return wcscasecmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
2228#else
2229 // Android, Mac OS X and Cygwin don't define wcscasecmp.
2230 // Other unknown OSes may not define it either.
2231 wint_t left, right;
2232 do {
2233 left = towlower(static_cast<wint_t>(*lhs++));
2234 right = towlower(static_cast<wint_t>(*rhs++));
2235 } while (left && left == right);
2236 return left == right;
2237#endif // OS selector
2238}

2240// Returns true if and only if str ends with the given suffix, ignoring case.
2241// Any string is considered to end with an empty suffix.
2242bool String::EndsWithCaseInsensitive(const std::string& str,
2243 const std::string& suffix) {
2244 const size_t str_len = str.length();
2245 const size_t suffix_len = suffix.length();
2246 return (str_len >= suffix_len) &&
2247 CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(str.c_str() + str_len - suffix_len,
2248 suffix.c_str());
2249}

2279 << static_cast<unsigned int>(value);

2283// Converts the buffer in a stringstream to an std::string, converting NUL
2284// bytes to "\\0" along the way.
2285std::string StringStreamToString(::std::stringstream* ss) {
2286 const ::std::string& str = ss->str();
2287 const char* const start = str.c_str();
2288 const char* const end = start + str.length();
2289
2290 std::string result;
2291 result.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(2 * (end - start)));
2292 for (const char* ch = start; ch != end; ++ch) {
2293 if (*ch == '\0') {
2294 result += "\\0"; // Replaces NUL with "\\0";
2295 } else {
2296 result += *ch;
2297 }
2298 }
2299
2300 return result;
2301}

2303// Appends the user-supplied message to the Google-Test-generated message.
2304std::string AppendUserMessage(const std::string& gtest_msg,
2305 const Message& user_msg) {
2306 // Appends the user message if it's non-empty.
2307 const std::string user_msg_string = user_msg.GetString();
2308 if (user_msg_string.empty()) {
2309 return gtest_msg;
2310 }
2311 if (gtest_msg.empty()) {
2312 return user_msg_string;
2313 }
2314 return gtest_msg + "\n" + user_msg_string;
2315}

2328// Returns the i-th test part result among all the results. i can

2330// aborts the program.

2352// Adds a test property to the list. If a property with the same key as the
2353// supplied property is already represented, the value of this test_property
2354// replaces the old value for that key.
2355void TestResult::RecordProperty(const std::string& xml_element,
2356 const TestProperty& test_property) {
2357 if (!ValidateTestProperty(xml_element, test_property)) {
2358 return;
2359 }
2360 internal::MutexLock lock(test_properties_mutex_);
2361 const std::vector<TestProperty>::iterator property_with_matching_key =
2362 std::find_if(test_properties_.begin(), test_properties_.end(),
2363 internal::TestPropertyKeyIs(test_property.key()));
2364 if (property_with_matching_key == test_properties_.end()) {
2365 test_properties_.push_back(test_property);
2366 return;
2367 }
2368 property_with_matching_key->SetValue(test_property.value());
2369}

2371// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testsuites> element of XML
2372// output.
2373static const char* const kReservedTestSuitesAttributes[] = {
2374 "disabled", "errors", "failures", "name",
2375 "random_seed", "tests", "time", "timestamp"};
2376
2377// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testsuite> element of XML
2378// output.
2379static const char* const kReservedTestSuiteAttributes[] = {
2380 "disabled", "errors", "failures", "name",
2381 "tests", "time", "timestamp", "skipped"};
2382
2383// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testcase> element of XML output.
2384static const char* const kReservedTestCaseAttributes[] = {
2385 "classname", "name", "status", "time",
2386 "type_param", "value_param", "file", "line"};
2387
2388// Use a slightly different set for allowed output to ensure existing tests can
2389// still RecordProperty("result") or RecordProperty("timestamp")
2390static const char* const kReservedOutputTestCaseAttributes[] = {
2391 "classname", "name", "status", "time", "type_param",
2392 "value_param", "file", "line", "result", "timestamp"};
2393
2394template <size_t kSize>
2395std::vector<std::string> ArrayAsVector(const char* const (&array)[kSize]) {
2396 return std::vector<std::string>(array, array + kSize);
2397}
2398
2399static std::vector<std::string> GetReservedAttributesForElement(
2400 const std::string& xml_element) {
2401 if (xml_element == "testsuites") {
2402 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuitesAttributes);
2403 } else if (xml_element == "testsuite") {
2404 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuiteAttributes);
2405 } else if (xml_element == "testcase") {
2406 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestCaseAttributes);
2407 } else {
2408 GTEST_CHECK_(false) << "Unrecognized xml_element provided: " << xml_element;
2409 }
2410 // This code is unreachable but some compilers may not realizes that.
2411 return std::vector<std::string>();
2412}
2413
2414#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
2415// TODO(jdesprez): Merge the two getReserved attributes once skip is improved
2416// This function is only used when file systems are enabled.
2417static std::vector<std::string> GetReservedOutputAttributesForElement(
2418 const std::string& xml_element) {
2419 if (xml_element == "testsuites") {
2420 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuitesAttributes);
2421 } else if (xml_element == "testsuite") {
2422 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuiteAttributes);
2423 } else if (xml_element == "testcase") {
2424 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedOutputTestCaseAttributes);
2425 } else {
2426 GTEST_CHECK_(false) << "Unrecognized xml_element provided: " << xml_element;
2427 }
2428 // This code is unreachable but some compilers may not realizes that.
2429 return std::vector<std::string>();
2430}
2431#endif

2433static std::string FormatWordList(const std::vector<std::string>& words) {
2434 Message word_list;
2435 for (size_t i = 0; i < words.size(); ++i) {
2436 if (i > 0 && words.size() > 2) {
2437 word_list << ", ";
2438 }
2439 if (i == words.size() - 1) {
2440 word_list << "and ";
2441 }
2442 word_list << "'" << words[i] << "'";
2443 }
2444 return word_list.GetString();
2445}

2447static bool ValidateTestPropertyName(
2448 const std::string& property_name,
2449 const std::vector<std::string>& reserved_names) {
2450 if (std::find(reserved_names.begin(), reserved_names.end(), property_name) !=
2451 reserved_names.end()) {
2452 ADD_FAILURE() << "Reserved key used in RecordProperty(): " << property_name
2453 << " (" << FormatWordList(reserved_names)
2454 << " are reserved by " << GTEST_NAME_ << ")";
2455 return false;
2456 }
2457 return true;
2458}

2460// Adds a failure if the key is a reserved attribute of the element named
2461// xml_element. Returns true if the property is valid.
2462bool TestResult::ValidateTestProperty(const std::string& xml_element,
2463 const TestProperty& test_property) {
2464 return ValidateTestPropertyName(test_property.key(),
2465 GetReservedAttributesForElement(xml_element));

2486// Returns true if and only if the test failed.
2487bool TestResult::Failed() const {
2488 for (int i = 0; i < total_part_count(); ++i) {
2489 if (GetTestPartResult(i).failed()) return true;
2490 }
2491 return false;

2496 return result.fatally_failed();

2499// Returns true if and only if the test fatally failed.
2500bool TestResult::HasFatalFailure() const {
2501 return CountIf(test_part_results_, TestPartFatallyFailed) > 0;
2502}

2504// Returns true if and only if the test part non-fatally failed.
2505static bool TestPartNonfatallyFailed(const TestPartResult& result) {
2506 return result.nonfatally_failed();

2508
2509// Returns true if and only if the test has a non-fatal failure.

2512}

2514// Gets the number of all test parts. This is the sum of the number
2515// of successful test parts and the number of failed test parts.

2568
2569// Google Test requires all tests in the same test suite to use the same test
2570// fixture class. This function checks if the current test has the
2571// same fixture class as the first test in the current test suite. If
2572// yes, it returns true; otherwise it generates a Google Test failure and
2573// returns false.
2574bool Test::HasSameFixtureClass() {
2575 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
2576 const TestSuite* const test_suite = impl->current_test_suite();
2577
2578 // Info about the first test in the current test suite.
2579 const TestInfo* const first_test_info = test_suite->test_info_list()[0];
2580 const internal::TypeId first_fixture_id = first_test_info->fixture_class_id_;
2581 const char* const first_test_name = first_test_info->name();
2582
2583 // Info about the current test.
2584 const TestInfo* const this_test_info = impl->current_test_info();
2585 const internal::TypeId this_fixture_id = this_test_info->fixture_class_id_;
2586 const char* const this_test_name = this_test_info->name();
2587
2588 if (this_fixture_id != first_fixture_id) {
2589 // Is the first test defined using TEST?
2590 const bool first_is_TEST = first_fixture_id == internal::GetTestTypeId();
2591 // Is this test defined using TEST?
2592 const bool this_is_TEST = this_fixture_id == internal::GetTestTypeId();
2593
2594 if (first_is_TEST || this_is_TEST) {
2595 // Both TEST and TEST_F appear in same test suite, which is incorrect.
2596 // Tell the user how to fix this.
2597
2598 // Gets the name of the TEST and the name of the TEST_F. Note
2599 // that first_is_TEST and this_is_TEST cannot both be true, as
2600 // the fixture IDs are different for the two tests.
2601 const char* const TEST_name =
2602 first_is_TEST ? first_test_name : this_test_name;
2603 const char* const TEST_F_name =
2604 first_is_TEST ? this_test_name : first_test_name;
2605
2606 ADD_FAILURE()
2607 << "All tests in the same test suite must use the same test fixture\n"
2608 << "class, so mixing TEST_F and TEST in the same test suite is\n"
2609 << "illegal. In test suite " << this_test_info->test_suite_name()
2610 << ",\n"
2611 << "test " << TEST_F_name << " is defined using TEST_F but\n"
2612 << "test " << TEST_name << " is defined using TEST. You probably\n"
2613 << "want to change the TEST to TEST_F or move it to another test\n"
2614 << "case.";
2615 } else {
2616 // Two fixture classes with the same name appear in two different
2617 // namespaces, which is not allowed. Tell the user how to fix this.
2618 ADD_FAILURE()
2619 << "All tests in the same test suite must use the same test fixture\n"
2620 << "class. However, in test suite "
2621 << this_test_info->test_suite_name() << ",\n"
2622 << "you defined test " << first_test_name << " and test "
2623 << this_test_name << "\n"
2624 << "using two different test fixture classes. This can happen if\n"
2625 << "the two classes are from different namespaces or translation\n"
2626 << "units and have the same name. You should probably rename one\n"
2627 << "of the classes to put the tests into different test suites.";
2628 }
2629 return false;
2630 }
2631
2632 return true;
2633}

2637#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
2638
2639// Adds an "exception thrown" fatal failure to the current test.
2640static std::string FormatCxxExceptionMessage(const char* description,
2641 const char* location) {
2642 Message message;
2643 if (description != nullptr) {
2644 message << "C++ exception with description \"" << description << "\"";
2645 } else {
2646 message << "Unknown C++ exception";
2647 }
2648 message << " thrown in " << location << ".";
2649
2650 return message.GetString();
2651}

2653static std::string PrintTestPartResultToString(
2654 const TestPartResult& test_part_result);
2655
2656GoogleTestFailureException::GoogleTestFailureException(
2657 const TestPartResult& failure)
2658 : ::std::runtime_error(PrintTestPartResultToString(failure).c_str()) {}
2659
2660#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
2661
2662// We put these helper functions in the internal namespace as IBM's xlC
2663// compiler rejects the code if they were declared static.
2664
2665// Runs the given method and handles SEH exceptions it throws, when
2666// SEH is supported; returns the 0-value for type Result in case of an
2667// SEH exception. (Microsoft compilers cannot handle SEH and C++
2668// exceptions in the same function. Therefore, we provide a separate
2669// wrapper function for handling SEH exceptions.)
2670template <class T, typename Result>
2671Result HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(T* object, Result (T::*method)(),
2672 const char* location) {
2673#if GTEST_HAS_SEH
2674 __try {
2675 return (object->*method)();
2676 } __except (internal::UnitTestOptions::GTestProcessSEH( // NOLINT
2677 GetExceptionCode(), location)) {
2678 return static_cast<Result>(0);
2679 }
2680#else
2681 (void)location;
2682 return (object->*method)();
2683#endif // GTEST_HAS_SEH
2684}
2685
2686// Runs the given method and catches and reports C++ and/or SEH-style
2687// exceptions, if they are supported; returns the 0-value for type
2688// Result in case of an SEH exception.
2689template <class T, typename Result>
2690Result HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(T* object, Result (T::*method)(),
2691 const char* location) {
2692 // NOTE: The user code can affect the way in which Google Test handles
2693 // exceptions by setting GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions), but only before
2694 // RUN_ALL_TESTS() starts. It is technically possible to check the flag
2695 // after the exception is caught and either report or re-throw the
2696 // exception based on the flag's value:
2697 //
2698 // try {
2699 // // Perform the test method.
2700 // } catch (...) {
2701 // if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(catch_exceptions))
2702 // // Report the exception as failure.
2703 // else
2704 // throw; // Re-throws the original exception.
2705 // }
2706 //
2707 // However, the purpose of this flag is to allow the program to drop into
2708 // the debugger when the exception is thrown. On most platforms, once the
2709 // control enters the catch block, the exception origin information is
2710 // lost and the debugger will stop the program at the point of the
2711 // re-throw in this function -- instead of at the point of the original
2712 // throw statement in the code under test. For this reason, we perform
2713 // the check early, sacrificing the ability to affect Google Test's
2714 // exception handling in the method where the exception is thrown.
2715 if (internal::GetUnitTestImpl()->catch_exceptions()) {
2716#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
2717 try {
2718 return HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(object, method, location);
2719 } catch (const AssertionException&) { // NOLINT
2720 // This failure was reported already.
2721 } catch (const internal::GoogleTestFailureException&) { // NOLINT
2722 // This exception type can only be thrown by a failed Google
2723 // Test assertion with the intention of letting another testing
2724 // framework catch it. Therefore we just re-throw it.
2725 throw;
2726 } catch (const std::exception& e) { // NOLINT
2727 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(
2728 TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
2729 FormatCxxExceptionMessage(e.what(), location));
2730 } catch (...) { // NOLINT
2731 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(
2732 TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
2733 FormatCxxExceptionMessage(nullptr, location));
2734 }
2735 return static_cast<Result>(0);
2736#else
2737 return HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(object, method, location);
2738#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
2739 } else {
2740 return (object->*method)();
2741 }
2742}
2743
2744} // namespace internal
2745
2746// Runs the test and updates the test result.
2747void Test::Run() {
2748 if (!HasSameFixtureClass()) return;
2749
2750 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
2751 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
2752 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(this, &Test::SetUp, "SetUp()");
2753 // We will run the test only if SetUp() was successful and didn't call
2754 // GTEST_SKIP().
2755 if (!HasFatalFailure() && !IsSkipped()) {
2756 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
2757 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(this, &Test::TestBody,
2758 "the test body");
2759 }
2760
2761 // However, we want to clean up as much as possible. Hence we will
2762 // always call TearDown(), even if SetUp() or the test body has
2763 // failed.
2764 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
2765 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(this, &Test::TearDown,
2766 "TearDown()");
2767}

2813// Creates a new TestInfo object and registers it with Google Test;
2814// returns the created object.
2815//
2816// Arguments:
2817//
2818// test_suite_name: name of the test suite
2819// name: name of the test
2820// type_param: the name of the test's type parameter, or NULL if
2821// this is not a typed or a type-parameterized test.
2822// value_param: text representation of the test's value parameter,
2823// or NULL if this is not a value-parameterized test.
2824// code_location: code location where the test is defined
2825// fixture_class_id: ID of the test fixture class
2826// set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test suite
2827// tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test suite
2828// factory: pointer to the factory that creates a test object.
2829// The newly created TestInfo instance will assume
2830// ownership of the factory object.
2831TestInfo* MakeAndRegisterTestInfo(
2832 std::string test_suite_name, const char* name, const char* type_param,
2833 const char* value_param, CodeLocation code_location,
2834 TypeId fixture_class_id, SetUpTestSuiteFunc set_up_tc,
2835 TearDownTestSuiteFunc tear_down_tc, TestFactoryBase* factory) {
2836 TestInfo* const test_info =
2837 new TestInfo(std::move(test_suite_name), name, type_param, value_param,
2838 std::move(code_location), fixture_class_id, factory);
2839 GetUnitTestImpl()->AddTestInfo(set_up_tc, tear_down_tc, test_info);
2840 return test_info;
2841}

2843void ReportInvalidTestSuiteType(const char* test_suite_name,
2844 const CodeLocation& code_location) {
2845 Message errors;
2846 errors
2847 << "Attempted redefinition of test suite " << test_suite_name << ".\n"
2848 << "All tests in the same test suite must use the same test fixture\n"
2849 << "class. However, in test suite " << test_suite_name << ", you tried\n"
2850 << "to define a test using a fixture class different from the one\n"
2851 << "used earlier. This can happen if the two fixture classes are\n"
2852 << "from different namespaces and have the same name. You should\n"
2853 << "probably rename one of the classes to put the tests into different\n"
2854 << "test suites.";
2855
2856 GTEST_LOG_(ERROR) << FormatFileLocation(code_location.file.c_str(),
2857 code_location.line)
2858 << " " << errors.GetString();

2873
2874// Creates the test object, runs it, records its result, and then
2875// deletes it.
2876void TestInfo::Run() {
2877 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
2878 if (!should_run_) {
2879 if (is_disabled_ && matches_filter_) repeater->OnTestDisabled(*this);
2880 return;
2881 }
2882
2883 // Tells UnitTest where to store test result.
2884 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_info(this);
2885
2886 // Notifies the unit test event listeners that a test is about to start.
2887 repeater->OnTestStart(*this);
2888 result_.set_start_timestamp(internal::GetTimeInMillis());
2889 internal::Timer timer;
2890 UnitTest::GetInstance()->UponLeavingGTest();
2891
2892 // Creates the test object.
2893 Test* const test = internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
2894 factory_, &internal::TestFactoryBase::CreateTest,
2895 "the test fixture's constructor");
2896
2897 // Runs the test if the constructor didn't generate a fatal failure or invoke
2898 // GTEST_SKIP().
2899 // Note that the object will not be null
2900 if (!Test::HasFatalFailure() && !Test::IsSkipped()) {
2901 // This doesn't throw as all user code that can throw are wrapped into
2902 // exception handling code.
2903 test->Run();
2904 }
2905
2906 if (test != nullptr) {
2907 // Deletes the test object.
2908 UnitTest::GetInstance()->UponLeavingGTest();
2909 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
2910 test, &Test::DeleteSelf_, "the test fixture's destructor");
2911 }
2912
2913 result_.set_elapsed_time(timer.Elapsed());
2914
2915 // Notifies the unit test event listener that a test has just finished.
2916 repeater->OnTestEnd(*this);
2917
2918 // Tells UnitTest to stop associating assertion results to this
2919 // test.
2920 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_info(nullptr);
2921}
2922
2923// Skip and records a skipped test result for this object.
2924void TestInfo::Skip() {
2925 if (!should_run_) return;
2926
2927 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_info(this);
2928
2929 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
2930
2931 // Notifies the unit test event listeners that a test is about to start.
2932 repeater->OnTestStart(*this);
2933
2934 const TestPartResult test_part_result =
2935 TestPartResult(TestPartResult::kSkip, this->file(), this->line(), "");
2936 internal::GetUnitTestImpl()
2937 ->GetTestPartResultReporterForCurrentThread()
2938 ->ReportTestPartResult(test_part_result);
2939
2940 // Notifies the unit test event listener that a test has just finished.
2941 repeater->OnTestEnd(*this);
2942 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_info(nullptr);
2943}

3028// destruction of the TestSuite object.
3029void TestSuite::AddTestInfo(TestInfo* test_info) {
3030 test_info_list_.push_back(test_info);
3031 test_indices_.push_back(static_cast<int>(test_indices_.size()));

3033
3034// Runs every test in this TestSuite.
3035void TestSuite::Run() {
3036 if (!should_run_) return;
3037
3038 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_suite(this);
3039
3040 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
3041
3042 // Ensure our tests are in a deterministic order.
3043 //
3044 // We do this by sorting lexicographically on (file, line number), providing
3045 // an order matching what the user can see in the source code.
3046 //
3047 // In the common case the line number comparison shouldn't be necessary,
3048 // because the registrations made by the TEST macro are executed in order
3049 // within a translation unit. But this is not true of the manual registration
3050 // API, and in more exotic scenarios a single file may be part of multiple
3051 // translation units.
3052 std::stable_sort(test_info_list_.begin(), test_info_list_.end(),
3053 [](const TestInfo* const a, const TestInfo* const b) {
3054 if (const int result = std::strcmp(a->file(), b->file())) {
3055 return result < 0;
3056 }
3057
3058 return a->line() < b->line();
3059 });
3060
3061 // Call both legacy and the new API
3062 repeater->OnTestSuiteStart(*this);
3063// Legacy API is deprecated but still available
3064#ifndef GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3065 repeater->OnTestCaseStart(*this);
3066#endif // GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3067
3068 UnitTest::GetInstance()->UponLeavingGTest();
3069 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
3070 this, &TestSuite::RunSetUpTestSuite, "SetUpTestSuite()");
3071
3072 const bool skip_all =
3073 ad_hoc_test_result().Failed() || ad_hoc_test_result().Skipped();
3074
3075 start_timestamp_ = internal::GetTimeInMillis();
3076 internal::Timer timer;
3077 for (int i = 0; i < total_test_count(); i++) {
3078 if (skip_all) {
3079 GetMutableTestInfo(i)->Skip();
3080 } else {
3081 GetMutableTestInfo(i)->Run();
3082 }
3083 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(fail_fast) &&
3084 GetMutableTestInfo(i)->result()->Failed()) {
3085 for (int j = i + 1; j < total_test_count(); j++) {
3086 GetMutableTestInfo(j)->Skip();
3087 }
3088 break;
3089 }
3090 }
3091 elapsed_time_ = timer.Elapsed();
3092
3093 UnitTest::GetInstance()->UponLeavingGTest();
3094 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
3095 this, &TestSuite::RunTearDownTestSuite, "TearDownTestSuite()");
3096
3097 // Call both legacy and the new API
3098 repeater->OnTestSuiteEnd(*this);
3099// Legacy API is deprecated but still available
3100#ifndef GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3101 repeater->OnTestCaseEnd(*this);
3102#endif // GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3103
3104 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_suite(nullptr);
3105}
3106
3107// Skips all tests under this TestSuite.
3108void TestSuite::Skip() {
3109 if (!should_run_) return;
3110
3111 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_suite(this);
3112
3113 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
3114
3115 // Call both legacy and the new API
3116 repeater->OnTestSuiteStart(*this);
3117// Legacy API is deprecated but still available
3118#ifndef GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3119 repeater->OnTestCaseStart(*this);
3120#endif // GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3121
3122 for (int i = 0; i < total_test_count(); i++) {
3123 GetMutableTestInfo(i)->Skip();
3124 }
3125
3126 // Call both legacy and the new API
3127 repeater->OnTestSuiteEnd(*this);
3128 // Legacy API is deprecated but still available
3129#ifndef GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3130 repeater->OnTestCaseEnd(*this);
3131#endif // GTEST_REMOVE_LEGACY_TEST_CASEAPI_
3132
3133 UnitTest::GetInstance()->set_current_test_suite(nullptr);
3134}
