5522
5523// Runs all tests in this UnitTest object and prints the result.
5524// Returns 0 if successful, or 1 otherwise.
5525//
5526// We don't protect this under mutex_, as we only support calling it
5527// from the main thread.
5528int UnitTest::Run() {
5529#ifdef GTEST_INTERNAL_HAS_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE
5530 const bool in_death_test_child_process =
5531 !GTEST_FLAG_GET(internal_run_death_test).empty();
5532
5533 // Google Test implements this protocol for catching that a test
5534 // program exits before returning control to Google Test:
5535 //
5536 // 1. Upon start, Google Test creates a file whose absolute path
5537 // is specified by the environment variable
5538 // TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE.
5539 // 2. When Google Test has finished its work, it deletes the file.
5540 //
5541 // This allows a test runner to set TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE before
5542 // running a Google-Test-based test program and check the existence
5543 // of the file at the end of the test execution to see if it has
5544 // exited prematurely.
5545
5546 // If we are in the child process of a death test, don't
5547 // create/delete the premature exit file, as doing so is unnecessary
5548 // and will confuse the parent process. Otherwise, create/delete
5549 // the file upon entering/leaving this function. If the program
5550 // somehow exits before this function has a chance to return, the
5551 // premature-exit file will be left undeleted, causing a test runner
5552 // that understands the premature-exit-file protocol to report the
5553 // test as having failed.
5554 const internal::ScopedPrematureExitFile premature_exit_file(
5555 in_death_test_child_process
5556 ? nullptr
5557 : internal::posix::GetEnv("TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE"));
5558#else
5559 const bool in_death_test_child_process = false;
5560#endif // GTEST_INTERNAL_HAS_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE
5561
5562 // Captures the value of GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions). This value will be
5563 // used for the duration of the program.
5564 impl()->set_catch_exceptions(GTEST_FLAG_GET(catch_exceptions));
5565
5566#ifdef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
5567 // Either the user wants Google Test to catch exceptions thrown by the
5568 // tests or this is executing in the context of death test child
5569 // process. In either case the user does not want to see pop-up dialogs
5570 // about crashes - they are expected.
5571 if (impl()->catch_exceptions() || in_death_test_child_process) {
5572#if !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE) && !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE) && \
5573 !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT) && !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_GAMES)
5574 // SetErrorMode doesn't exist on CE.
5575 SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOALIGNMENTFAULTEXCEPT |
5576 SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX | SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX);
5577#endif // !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
5578
5579#if (defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW)) && \
5580 !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE)
5581 // Death test children can be terminated with _abort(). On Windows,
5582 // _abort() can show a dialog with a warning message. This forces the
5583 // abort message to go to stderr instead.
5584 _set_error_mode(_OUT_TO_STDERR);
5585#endif
5586
5587#if defined(_MSC_VER) && !defined(GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE)
5588 // In the debug version, Visual Studio pops up a separate dialog
5589 // offering a choice to debug the aborted program. We need to suppress
5590 // this dialog or it will pop up for every EXPECT/ASSERT_DEATH statement
5591 // executed. Google Test will notify the user of any unexpected
5592 // failure via stderr.
5593 if (!GTEST_FLAG_GET(break_on_failure))
5594 _set_abort_behavior(
5595 0x0, // Clear the following flags:
5596 _WRITE_ABORT_MSG | _CALL_REPORTFAULT); // pop-up window, core dump.
5597
5598 // In debug mode, the Windows CRT can crash with an assertion over invalid
5599 // input (e.g. passing an invalid file descriptor). The default handling
5600 // for these assertions is to pop up a dialog and wait for user input.
5601 // Instead ask the CRT to dump such assertions to stderr non-interactively.
5602 if (!IsDebuggerPresent()) {
5603 (void)_CrtSetReportMode(_CRT_ASSERT,
5604 _CRTDBG_MODE_FILE | _CRTDBG_MODE_DEBUG);
5605 (void)_CrtSetReportFile(_CRT_ASSERT, _CRTDBG_FILE_STDERR);
5606 }
5607#endif
5608 }
5609#else
5610 (void)in_death_test_child_process; // Needed inside the #if block above
5611#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
5612
5613 return internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
5614 impl(), &internal::UnitTestImpl::RunAllTests,
5615 "auxiliary test code (environments or event listeners)")
5616 ? 0
5617 : 1;
5618}

5724// Adds a TestProperty to the current TestResult object when invoked in a
5725// context of a test, to current test suite's ad_hoc_test_result when invoke
5726// from SetUpTestSuite/TearDownTestSuite, or to the global property set
5727// otherwise. If the result already contains a property with the same key,
5728// the value will be updated.
5729void UnitTestImpl::RecordProperty(const TestProperty& test_property) {
5730 std::string xml_element;
5731 TestResult* test_result; // TestResult appropriate for property recording.
5732
5733 if (current_test_info_ != nullptr) {
5734 xml_element = "testcase";
5735 test_result = &(current_test_info_->result_);
5736 } else if (current_test_suite_ != nullptr) {
5737 xml_element = "testsuite";
5738 test_result = &(current_test_suite_->ad_hoc_test_result_);
5739 } else {
5740 xml_element = "testsuites";
5741 test_result = &ad_hoc_test_result_;
5742 }
5743 test_result->RecordProperty(xml_element, test_property);
5744}

5779// Initializes event listeners for streaming test results in string form.
5780// Must not be called before InitGoogleTest.
5781void UnitTestImpl::ConfigureStreamingOutput() {

5783 if (!target.empty()) {

5785 if (pos != std::string::npos) {
5786 listeners()->Append(

5790 << "\" ignored.";

5795
5796// Performs initialization dependent upon flag values obtained in
5797// ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly. Is called from InitGoogleTest after the call to
5798// ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly. In case a user neglects to call InitGoogleTest
5799// this function is also called from RunAllTests. Since this function can be
5800// called more than once, it has to be idempotent.
5801void UnitTestImpl::PostFlagParsingInit() {
5802 // Ensures that this function does not execute more than once.
5803 if (!post_flag_parse_init_performed_) {
5804 post_flag_parse_init_performed_ = true;
5805
5806#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_)
5807 // Register to send notifications about key process state changes.
5808 listeners()->Append(new GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_());
5809#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_)
5810
5811#ifdef GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
5812 InitDeathTestSubprocessControlInfo();
5813 SuppressTestEventsIfInSubprocess();
5814#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
5815
5816 // Registers parameterized tests. This makes parameterized tests
5817 // available to the UnitTest reflection API without running
5818 // RUN_ALL_TESTS.
5819 RegisterParameterizedTests();
5820
5821 // Configures listeners for XML output. This makes it possible for users
5822 // to shut down the default XML output before invoking RUN_ALL_TESTS.
5823 ConfigureXmlOutput();
5824
5825 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(brief)) {
5826 listeners()->SetDefaultResultPrinter(new BriefUnitTestResultPrinter);
5827 }
5828
5829#if GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
5830 // Configures listeners for streaming test results to the specified server.
5831 ConfigureStreamingOutput();
5832#endif // GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
5833
5834#ifdef GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5835 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(install_failure_signal_handler)) {
5836 absl::FailureSignalHandlerOptions options;
5837 absl::InstallFailureSignalHandler(options);
5838 }
5839#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5840 }
5841}
5842
5843// Finds and returns a TestSuite with the given name. If one doesn't
5844// exist, creates one and returns it. It's the CALLER'S
5845// RESPONSIBILITY to ensure that this function is only called WHEN THE
5846// TESTS ARE NOT SHUFFLED.
5847//
5848// Arguments:
5849//
5850// test_suite_name: name of the test suite
5851// type_param: the name of the test suite's type parameter, or NULL if
5852// this is not a typed or a type-parameterized test suite.
5853// set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test suite
5854// tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test suite
5855TestSuite* UnitTestImpl::GetTestSuite(
5856 const std::string& test_suite_name, const char* type_param,
5857 internal::SetUpTestSuiteFunc set_up_tc,
5858 internal::TearDownTestSuiteFunc tear_down_tc) {
5859 // During initialization, all TestInfos for a given suite are added in
5860 // sequence. To optimize this case, see if the most recently added suite is
5861 // the one being requested now.
5862 if (!test_suites_.empty() &&
5863 (*test_suites_.rbegin())->name_ == test_suite_name) {
5864 return *test_suites_.rbegin();
5865 }
5866
5867 // Fall back to searching the collection.
5868 auto item_it = test_suites_by_name_.find(test_suite_name);
5869 if (item_it != test_suites_by_name_.end()) {
5870 return item_it->second;
5871 }
5872
5873 // Not found. Create a new instance.
5874 auto* const new_test_suite =
5875 new TestSuite(test_suite_name, type_param, set_up_tc, tear_down_tc);
5876 test_suites_by_name_.emplace(test_suite_name, new_test_suite);
5877
5878 const UnitTestFilter death_test_suite_filter(kDeathTestSuiteFilter);
5879 // Is this a death test suite?
5880 if (death_test_suite_filter.MatchesName(test_suite_name)) {
5881 // Yes. Inserts the test suite after the last death test suite
5882 // defined so far. This only works when the test suites haven't
5883 // been shuffled. Otherwise we may end up running a death test
5884 // after a non-death test.
5885 ++last_death_test_suite_;
5886 test_suites_.insert(test_suites_.begin() + last_death_test_suite_,
5887 new_test_suite);
5888 } else {
5889 // No. Appends to the end of the list.
5890 test_suites_.push_back(new_test_suite);
5891 }
5892
5893 test_suite_indices_.push_back(static_cast<int>(test_suite_indices_.size()));
5894 return new_test_suite;
5895}
5896
5897// Helpers for setting up / tearing down the given environment. They
5898// are for use in the ForEach() function.
5899static void SetUpEnvironment(Environment* env) { env->SetUp(); }
5900static void TearDownEnvironment(Environment* env) { env->TearDown(); }
5901
5902// If the environment variable TEST_WARNINGS_OUTPUT_FILE was provided, appends
5903// `str` to the file, creating the file if necessary.
5904#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5905static void AppendToTestWarningsOutputFile(const std::string& str) {
5906 const char* const filename = posix::GetEnv(kTestWarningsOutputFile);
5907 if (filename == nullptr) {
5908 return;
5909 }
5910 auto* const file = posix::FOpen(filename, "a");
5911 if (file == nullptr) {
5912 return;
5913 }
5914 GTEST_CHECK_(fwrite(str.data(), 1, str.size(), file) == str.size());
5915 GTEST_CHECK_(posix::FClose(file) == 0);
5916}
5917#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5918
5919// Runs all tests in this UnitTest object, prints the result, and
5920// returns true if all tests are successful. If any exception is
5921// thrown during a test, the test is considered to be failed, but the
5922// rest of the tests will still be run.
5923//
5924// When parameterized tests are enabled, it expands and registers
5925// parameterized tests first in RegisterParameterizedTests().
5926// All other functions called from RunAllTests() may safely assume that
5927// parameterized tests are ready to be counted and run.
5928bool UnitTestImpl::RunAllTests() {
5929 // True if and only if Google Test is initialized before RUN_ALL_TESTS() is
5930 // called.
5931 const bool gtest_is_initialized_before_run_all_tests = GTestIsInitialized();
5932
5933 // Do not run any test if the --help flag was specified.
5934 if (g_help_flag) return true;
5935
5936 // Repeats the call to the post-flag parsing initialization in case the
5937 // user didn't call InitGoogleTest.
5938 PostFlagParsingInit();
5939
5940 // Handle the case where the program has no tests linked.
5941 // Sometimes this is a programmer mistake, but sometimes it is intended.
5942 if (total_test_count() == 0) {
5943 constexpr char kNoTestLinkedMessage[] =
5944 "This test program does NOT link in any test case.";
5945 constexpr char kNoTestLinkedFatal[] =
5946 "This is INVALID. Please make sure to link in at least one test case.";
5947 constexpr char kNoTestLinkedWarning[] =
5948 "Please make sure this is intended.";
5949 const bool fail_if_no_test_linked = GTEST_FLAG_GET(fail_if_no_test_linked);
5950 ColoredPrintf(
5951 GTestColor::kRed, "%s %s\n", kNoTestLinkedMessage,
5952 fail_if_no_test_linked ? kNoTestLinkedFatal : kNoTestLinkedWarning);
5953 if (fail_if_no_test_linked) {
5954 return false;
5955 }
5956#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5957 AppendToTestWarningsOutputFile(std::string(kNoTestLinkedMessage) + ' ' +
5958 kNoTestLinkedWarning + '\n');
5959#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5960 }
5961
5962#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5963 // Even if sharding is not on, test runners may want to use the
5964 // GTEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE to query whether the test supports the sharding
5965 // protocol.
5966 internal::WriteToShardStatusFileIfNeeded();
5967#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
5968
5969 // True if and only if we are in a subprocess for running a thread-safe-style
5970 // death test.
5971 bool in_subprocess_for_death_test = false;
5972
5973#ifdef GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
5974 in_subprocess_for_death_test = (internal_run_death_test_flag_ != nullptr);
5975#if defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_)
5976 if (in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
5977 GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_();
5978 }
5979#endif // defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_)
5980#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
5981
5982 const bool should_shard = ShouldShard(kTestTotalShards, kTestShardIndex,
5983 in_subprocess_for_death_test);
5984
5985 // Compares the full test names with the filter to decide which
5986 // tests to run.
5987 const bool has_tests_to_run =
5988 FilterTests(should_shard ? HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL
5989 : IGNORE_SHARDING_PROTOCOL) > 0;
5990
5991 // Lists the tests and exits if the --gtest_list_tests flag was specified.
5992 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(list_tests)) {
5993 // This must be called *after* FilterTests() has been called.
5994 ListTestsMatchingFilter();
5995 return true;
5996 }
5997
5998 random_seed_ = GetRandomSeedFromFlag(GTEST_FLAG_GET(random_seed));
5999
6000 // True if and only if at least one test has failed.
6001 bool failed = false;
6002
6003 TestEventListener* repeater = listeners()->repeater();
6004
6005 start_timestamp_ = GetTimeInMillis();
6006 repeater->OnTestProgramStart(*parent_);
6007
6008 // How many times to repeat the tests? We don't want to repeat them
6009 // when we are inside the subprocess of a death test.
6010 const int repeat = in_subprocess_for_death_test ? 1 : GTEST_FLAG_GET(repeat);
6011
6012 // Repeats forever if the repeat count is negative.
6013 const bool gtest_repeat_forever = repeat < 0;
6014
6015 // Should test environments be set up and torn down for each repeat, or only
6016 // set up on the first and torn down on the last iteration? If there is no
6017 // "last" iteration because the tests will repeat forever, always recreate the
6018 // environments to avoid leaks in case one of the environments is using
6019 // resources that are external to this process. Without this check there would
6020 // be no way to clean up those external resources automatically.
6021 const bool recreate_environments_when_repeating =
6022 GTEST_FLAG_GET(recreate_environments_when_repeating) ||
6023 gtest_repeat_forever;
6024
6025 for (int i = 0; gtest_repeat_forever || i != repeat; i++) {
6026 // We want to preserve failures generated by ad-hoc test
6027 // assertions executed before RUN_ALL_TESTS().
6028 ClearNonAdHocTestResult();
6029
6030 Timer timer;
6031
6032 // Shuffles test suites and tests if requested.
6033 if (has_tests_to_run && GTEST_FLAG_GET(shuffle)) {
6034 random()->Reseed(static_cast<uint32_t>(random_seed_));
6035 // This should be done before calling OnTestIterationStart(),
6036 // such that a test event listener can see the actual test order
6037 // in the event.
6038 ShuffleTests();
6039 }
6040
6041 // Tells the unit test event listeners that the tests are about to start.
6042 repeater->OnTestIterationStart(*parent_, i);
6043
6044 // Runs each test suite if there is at least one test to run.
6045 if (has_tests_to_run) {
6046 // Sets up all environments beforehand. If test environments aren't
6047 // recreated for each iteration, only do so on the first iteration.
6048 if (i == 0 || recreate_environments_when_repeating) {
6049 repeater->OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(*parent_);
6050 ForEach(environments_, SetUpEnvironment);
6051 repeater->OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(*parent_);
6052 }
6053
6054 // Runs the tests only if there was no fatal failure or skip triggered
6055 // during global set-up.
6056 if (Test::IsSkipped()) {
6057 // Emit diagnostics when global set-up calls skip, as it will not be
6058 // emitted by default.
6059 TestResult& test_result =
6060 *internal::GetUnitTestImpl()->current_test_result();
6061 for (int j = 0; j < test_result.total_part_count(); ++j) {
6062 const TestPartResult& test_part_result =
6063 test_result.GetTestPartResult(j);
6064 if (test_part_result.type() == TestPartResult::kSkip) {
6065 const std::string& result = test_part_result.message();
6066 printf("%s\n", result.c_str());
6067 }
6068 }
6069 fflush(stdout);
6070 } else if (!Test::HasFatalFailure()) {
6071 for (int test_index = 0; test_index < total_test_suite_count();
6072 test_index++) {
6073 GetMutableSuiteCase(test_index)->Run();
6074 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(fail_fast) &&
6075 GetMutableSuiteCase(test_index)->Failed()) {
6076 for (int j = test_index + 1; j < total_test_suite_count(); j++) {
6077 GetMutableSuiteCase(j)->Skip();
6078 }
6079 break;
6080 }
6081 }
6082 } else if (Test::HasFatalFailure()) {
6083 // If there was a fatal failure during the global setup then we know we
6084 // aren't going to run any tests. Explicitly mark all of the tests as
6085 // skipped to make this obvious in the output.
6086 for (int test_index = 0; test_index < total_test_suite_count();
6087 test_index++) {
6088 GetMutableSuiteCase(test_index)->Skip();
6089 }
6090 }
6091
6092 // Tears down all environments in reverse order afterwards. If test
6093 // environments aren't recreated for each iteration, only do so on the
6094 // last iteration.
6095 if (i == repeat - 1 || recreate_environments_when_repeating) {
6096 repeater->OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(*parent_);
6097 std::for_each(environments_.rbegin(), environments_.rend(),
6098 TearDownEnvironment);
6099 repeater->OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(*parent_);
6100 }
6101 } else if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(fail_if_no_test_selected)) {
6102 // If there were no tests to run, bail if we were requested to be
6103 // strict.
6104 constexpr char kNoTestsSelectedMessage[] =
6105 "No tests ran. Check that tests exist and are not disabled or "
6106 "filtered out.\n\n"
6107 "For sharded runs, this error indicates an empty shard. This can "
6108 "happen if you have more shards than tests, or if --gtest_filter "
6109 "leaves a shard with no tests.\n\n"
6110 "To permit empty shards (e.g., when debugging with a filter), "
6111 "specify \n"
6112 "--gtest_fail_if_no_test_selected=false.";
6113 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed, "%s\n", kNoTestsSelectedMessage);
6114 return false;
6115 }
6116
6117 elapsed_time_ = timer.Elapsed();
6118
6119 // Tells the unit test event listener that the tests have just finished.
6120 repeater->OnTestIterationEnd(*parent_, i);
6121
6122 // Gets the result and clears it.
6123 if (!Passed()) {
6124 failed = true;
6125 }
6126
6127 // Restores the original test order after the iteration. This
6128 // allows the user to quickly repro a failure that happens in the
6129 // N-th iteration without repeating the first (N - 1) iterations.
6130 // This is not enclosed in "if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) { ... }", in
6131 // case the user somehow changes the value of the flag somewhere
6132 // (it's always safe to unshuffle the tests).
6133 UnshuffleTests();
6134
6135 if (GTEST_FLAG_GET(shuffle)) {
6136 // Picks a new random seed for each iteration.
6137 random_seed_ = GetNextRandomSeed(random_seed_);
6138 }
6139 }
6140
6141 repeater->OnTestProgramEnd(*parent_);
6142 // Destroy environments in normal code, not in static teardown.
6143 bool delete_environment_on_teardown = true;
6144 if (delete_environment_on_teardown) {
6145 ForEach(environments_, internal::Delete<Environment>);
6146 environments_.clear();
6147 }
6148
6149 // Try to warn the user if no tests matched the test filter.
6150 if (ShouldWarnIfNoTestsMatchFilter()) {
6151 const std::string filter_warning =
6152 std::string("filter \"") + GTEST_FLAG_GET(filter) +
6153 "\" did not match any test; no tests were run\n";
6154 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed, "WARNING: %s", filter_warning.c_str());
6155#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6156 AppendToTestWarningsOutputFile(filter_warning);
6157#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6158 }
6159
6160 if (!gtest_is_initialized_before_run_all_tests) {
6161 ColoredPrintf(
6162 GTestColor::kRed,
6163 "\nIMPORTANT NOTICE - DO NOT IGNORE:\n"
6164 "This test program did NOT call " GTEST_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_NAME_
6165 "() before calling RUN_ALL_TESTS(). This is INVALID. Soon " GTEST_NAME_
6166 " will start to enforce the valid usage. "
6167 "Please fix it ASAP, or IT WILL START TO FAIL.\n"); // NOLINT
6168 }
6169
6170 return !failed;
6171}

6173#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6174// Reads the GTEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE environment variable, and creates the file
6175// if the variable is present. If a file already exists at this location, this
6176// function will write over it. If the variable is present, but the file cannot
6177// be created, prints an error and exits.
6178void WriteToShardStatusFileIfNeeded() {
6179 const char* const test_shard_file = posix::GetEnv(kTestShardStatusFile);
6180 if (test_shard_file != nullptr) {
6181 FILE* const file = posix::FOpen(test_shard_file, "w");
6182 if (file == nullptr) {
6183 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed,
6184 "Could not write to the test shard status file \"%s\" "
6185 "specified by the %s environment variable.\n",
6186 test_shard_file, kTestShardStatusFile);
6187 fflush(stdout);
6188 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6189 }
6190 fclose(file);
6191 }
6192}
6193#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6194
6195// Checks whether sharding is enabled by examining the relevant
6196// environment variable values. If the variables are present,
6197// but inconsistent (i.e., shard_index >= total_shards), prints
6198// an error and exits. If in_subprocess_for_death_test, sharding is
6199// disabled because it must only be applied to the original test
6200// process. Otherwise, we could filter out death tests we intended to execute.
6201bool ShouldShard(const char* total_shards_env, const char* shard_index_env,
6202 bool in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
6203 if (in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
6204 return false;
6205 }
6206
6207 const int32_t total_shards = Int32FromEnvOrDie(total_shards_env, -1);
6208 const int32_t shard_index = Int32FromEnvOrDie(shard_index_env, -1);
6209
6210 if (total_shards == -1 && shard_index == -1) {
6211 return false;
6212 } else if (total_shards == -1 && shard_index != -1) {
6213 const Message msg = Message() << "Invalid environment variables: you have "
6214 << kTestShardIndex << " = " << shard_index
6215 << ", but have left " << kTestTotalShards
6216 << " unset.\n";
6217 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed, "%s", msg.GetString().c_str());
6218 fflush(stdout);
6219 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6220 } else if (total_shards != -1 && shard_index == -1) {
6221 const Message msg = Message()
6222 << "Invalid environment variables: you have "
6223 << kTestTotalShards << " = " << total_shards
6224 << ", but have left " << kTestShardIndex << " unset.\n";
6225 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed, "%s", msg.GetString().c_str());
6226 fflush(stdout);
6227 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6228 } else if (shard_index < 0 || shard_index >= total_shards) {
6229 const Message msg =
6230 Message() << "Invalid environment variables: we require 0 <= "
6231 << kTestShardIndex << " < " << kTestTotalShards
6232 << ", but you have " << kTestShardIndex << "=" << shard_index
6233 << ", " << kTestTotalShards << "=" << total_shards << ".\n";
6234 ColoredPrintf(GTestColor::kRed, "%s", msg.GetString().c_str());
6235 fflush(stdout);
6236 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6237 }
6238
6239 return total_shards > 1;
6240}
6241
6242// Parses the environment variable var as an Int32. If it is unset,
6243// returns default_val. If it is not an Int32, prints an error
6244// and aborts.
6245int32_t Int32FromEnvOrDie(const char* var, int32_t default_val) {
6246 const char* str_val = posix::GetEnv(var);
6247 if (str_val == nullptr) {
6248 return default_val;
6249 }
6250
6251 int32_t result;
6252 if (!ParseInt32(Message() << "The value of environment variable " << var,
6253 str_val, &result)) {
6254 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6255 }
6256 return result;
6257}
6258
6259// Given the total number of shards, the shard index, and the test id,
6260// returns true if and only if the test should be run on this shard. The test id
6261// is some arbitrary but unique non-negative integer assigned to each test
6262// method. Assumes that 0 <= shard_index < total_shards.
6263bool ShouldRunTestOnShard(int total_shards, int shard_index, int test_id) {
6264 return (test_id % total_shards) == shard_index;
6265}
6266
6267// Compares the name of each test with the user-specified filter to
6268// decide whether the test should be run, then records the result in
6269// each TestSuite and TestInfo object.
6270// If shard_tests == true, further filters tests based on sharding
6271// variables in the environment - see
6272// https://github.com/google/googletest/blob/main/docs/advanced.md
6273// . Returns the number of tests that should run.
6274int UnitTestImpl::FilterTests(ReactionToSharding shard_tests) {
6275 const int32_t total_shards = shard_tests == HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL
6276 ? Int32FromEnvOrDie(kTestTotalShards, -1)
6277 : -1;
6278 const int32_t shard_index = shard_tests == HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL
6279 ? Int32FromEnvOrDie(kTestShardIndex, -1)
6280 : -1;
6281
6282 const PositiveAndNegativeUnitTestFilter gtest_flag_filter(
6283 GTEST_FLAG_GET(filter));
6284 const UnitTestFilter disable_test_filter(kDisableTestFilter);
6285 // num_runnable_tests are the number of tests that will
6286 // run across all shards (i.e., match filter and are not disabled).
6287 // num_selected_tests are the number of tests to be run on
6288 // this shard.
6289 int num_runnable_tests = 0;
6290 int num_selected_tests = 0;
6291 for (auto* test_suite : test_suites_) {
6292 const std::string& test_suite_name = test_suite->name_;
6293 test_suite->set_should_run(false);
6294
6295 for (TestInfo* test_info : test_suite->test_info_list()) {
6296 const std::string& test_name = test_info->name_;
6297 // A test is disabled if test suite name or test name matches
6298 // kDisableTestFilter.
6299 const bool is_disabled =
6300 disable_test_filter.MatchesName(test_suite_name) ||
6301 disable_test_filter.MatchesName(test_name);
6302 test_info->is_disabled_ = is_disabled;
6303
6304 const bool matches_filter =
6305 gtest_flag_filter.MatchesTest(test_suite_name, test_name);
6306 test_info->matches_filter_ = matches_filter;
6307
6308 const bool is_runnable =
6309 (GTEST_FLAG_GET(also_run_disabled_tests) || !is_disabled) &&
6310 matches_filter;
6311
6312 const bool is_in_another_shard =
6313 shard_tests != IGNORE_SHARDING_PROTOCOL &&
6314 !ShouldRunTestOnShard(total_shards, shard_index, num_runnable_tests);
6315 test_info->is_in_another_shard_ = is_in_another_shard;
6316 const bool is_selected = is_runnable && !is_in_another_shard;
6317
6318 num_runnable_tests += is_runnable;
6319 num_selected_tests += is_selected;
6320
6321 test_info->should_run_ = is_selected;
6322 test_suite->set_should_run(test_suite->should_run() || is_selected);
6323 }
6324 }
6325 return num_selected_tests;
6326}
6327
6328// Returns true if a warning should be issued if no tests match the test filter
6329// flag. We can't simply count the number of tests that ran because, for
6330// instance, test sharding and death tests might mean no tests are expected to
6331// run in this process, but will run in another process.
6332bool UnitTestImpl::ShouldWarnIfNoTestsMatchFilter() const {
6333 if (total_test_count() == 0) {
6334 // No tests were linked in to program.
6335 // This case is handled by a different warning.
6336 return false;
6337 }
6338 const PositiveAndNegativeUnitTestFilter gtest_flag_filter(
6339 GTEST_FLAG_GET(filter));
6340 for (auto* test_suite : test_suites_) {
6341 const std::string& test_suite_name = test_suite->name_;
6342 for (TestInfo* test_info : test_suite->test_info_list()) {
6343 const std::string& test_name = test_info->name_;
6344 if (gtest_flag_filter.MatchesTest(test_suite_name, test_name)) {
6345 return false;
6346 }
6347 }
6348 }
6349 return true;
6350}
6351
6352// Prints the given C-string on a single line by replacing all '\n'
6353// characters with string "\\n". If the output takes more than
6354// max_length characters, only prints the first max_length characters
6355// and "...".
6356static void PrintOnOneLine(const char* str, int max_length) {
6357 if (str != nullptr) {
6358 for (int i = 0; *str != '\0'; ++str) {
6359 if (i >= max_length) {
6360 printf("...");
6361 break;
6362 }
6363 if (*str == '\n') {
6364 printf("\\n");
6365 i += 2;
6366 } else {
6367 printf("%c", *str);
6368 ++i;
6369 }
6370 }
6371 }
6372}
6373
6374// Prints the names of the tests matching the user-specified filter flag.
6375void UnitTestImpl::ListTestsMatchingFilter() {
6376 // Print at most this many characters for each type/value parameter.
6377 const int kMaxParamLength = 250;
6378
6379 for (auto* test_suite : test_suites_) {
6380 bool printed_test_suite_name = false;
6381
6382 for (size_t j = 0; j < test_suite->test_info_list().size(); j++) {
6383 const TestInfo* const test_info = test_suite->test_info_list()[j];
6384 if (test_info->matches_filter_) {
6385 if (!printed_test_suite_name) {
6386 printed_test_suite_name = true;
6387 printf("%s.", test_suite->name());
6388 if (test_suite->type_param() != nullptr) {
6389 printf(" # %s = ", kTypeParamLabel);
6390 // We print the type parameter on a single line to make
6391 // the output easy to parse by a program.
6392 PrintOnOneLine(test_suite->type_param(), kMaxParamLength);
6393 }
6394 printf("\n");
6395 }
6396 printf(" %s", test_info->name());
6397 if (test_info->value_param() != nullptr) {
6398 printf(" # %s = ", kValueParamLabel);
6399 // We print the value parameter on a single line to make the
6400 // output easy to parse by a program.
6401 PrintOnOneLine(test_info->value_param(), kMaxParamLength);
6402 }
6403 printf("\n");
6404 }
6405 }
6406 }
6407 fflush(stdout);
6408#if GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6409 const std::string& output_format = UnitTestOptions::GetOutputFormat();
6410 if (output_format == "xml" || output_format == "json") {
6411 FILE* fileout =
6412 OpenFileForWriting(UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile());
6413 std::stringstream stream;
6414 if (output_format == "xml") {
6415 XmlUnitTestResultPrinter(
6416 UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile().c_str())
6417 .PrintXmlTestsList(&stream, test_suites_);
6418 } else if (output_format == "json") {
6419 JsonUnitTestResultPrinter(
6420 UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile().c_str())
6421 .PrintJsonTestList(&stream, test_suites_);
6422 }
6423 fprintf(fileout, "%s", StringStreamToString(&stream).c_str());
6424 fclose(fileout);
6425 }
6426#endif // GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6427}

6468// Shuffles all test suites, and the tests within each test suite,
6469// making sure that death tests are still run first.
6470void UnitTestImpl::ShuffleTests() {
6471 // Shuffles the death test suites.
6472 ShuffleRange(random(), 0, last_death_test_suite_ + 1, &test_suite_indices_);
6473
6474 // Shuffles the non-death test suites.
6475 ShuffleRange(random(), last_death_test_suite_ + 1,
6476 static_cast<int>(test_suites_.size()), &test_suite_indices_);
6477
6478 // Shuffles the tests inside each test suite.
6479 for (auto& test_suite : test_suites_) {
6480 test_suite->ShuffleTests(random());
6481 }
6482}
6483
6484// Restores the test suites and tests to their order before the first shuffle.
6485void UnitTestImpl::UnshuffleTests() {
6486 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_suites_.size(); i++) {
6487 // Unshuffles the tests in each test suite.
6488 test_suites_[i]->UnshuffleTests();
6489 // Resets the index of each test suite.
6490 test_suite_indices_[i] = static_cast<int>(i);
6491 }
6492}

6494// Returns the current OS stack trace as an std::string.
6495//
6496// The maximum number of stack frames to be included is specified by
6497// the gtest_stack_trace_depth flag. The skip_count parameter
6498// specifies the number of top frames to be skipped, which doesn't
6499// count against the number of frames to be included.
6500//
6501// For example, if Foo() calls Bar(), which in turn calls
6502// GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(..., 1), Foo() will be included in
6503// the trace but Bar() and GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop() won't.
6504GTEST_NO_INLINE_ GTEST_NO_TAIL_CALL_ std::string
6505GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(int skip_count) {
6506 // We pass skip_count + 1 to skip this wrapper function in addition
6507 // to what the user really wants to skip.
6508 return GetUnitTestImpl()->CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(skip_count + 1);
6509}
6510
6511// Used by the GTEST_SUPPRESS_UNREACHABLE_CODE_WARNING_BELOW_ macro to
6512// suppress unreachable code warnings.
6513namespace {
6514class ClassUniqueToAlwaysTrue {};
6515} // namespace
6516
6517bool IsTrue(bool condition) { return condition; }
6518
6519bool AlwaysTrue() {
6520#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
6521 // This condition is always false so AlwaysTrue() never actually throws,
6522 // but it makes the compiler think that it may throw.
6523 if (IsTrue(false)) throw ClassUniqueToAlwaysTrue();
6524#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
6525 return true;
6526}
6527
6528// If *pstr starts with the given prefix, modifies *pstr to be right
6529// past the prefix and returns true; otherwise leaves *pstr unchanged
6530// and returns false. None of pstr, *pstr, and prefix can be NULL.
6531bool SkipPrefix(const char* prefix, const char** pstr) {
6532 const size_t prefix_len = strlen(prefix);
6533 if (strncmp(*pstr, prefix, prefix_len) == 0) {
6534 *pstr += prefix_len;
6535 return true;
6536 }
6537 return false;
6538}
6539
6540// Parses a string as a command line flag. The string should have
6541// the format "--flag=value". When def_optional is true, the "=value"
6542// part can be omitted.
6543//
6544// Returns the value of the flag, or NULL if the parsing failed.
6545static const char* ParseFlagValue(const char* str, const char* flag_name,
6546 bool def_optional) {
6547 // str and flag must not be NULL.
6548 if (str == nullptr || flag_name == nullptr) return nullptr;
6549
6550 // The flag must start with "--" followed by GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_.
6551 const std::string flag_str =
6552 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + flag_name;
6553 const size_t flag_len = flag_str.length();
6554 if (strncmp(str, flag_str.c_str(), flag_len) != 0) return nullptr;
6555
6556 // Skips the flag name.
6557 const char* flag_end = str + flag_len;
6558
6559 // When def_optional is true, it's OK to not have a "=value" part.
6560 if (def_optional && (flag_end[0] == '\0')) {
6561 return flag_end;
6562 }
6563
6564 // If def_optional is true and there are more characters after the
6565 // flag name, or if def_optional is false, there must be a '=' after
6566 // the flag name.
6567 if (flag_end[0] != '=') return nullptr;
6568
6569 // Returns the string after "=".
6570 return flag_end + 1;
6571}
6572
6573// Parses a string for a bool flag, in the form of either
6574// "--flag=value" or "--flag".
6575//
6576// In the former case, the value is taken as true as long as it does
6577// not start with '0', 'f', or 'F'.
6578//
6579// In the latter case, the value is taken as true.
6580//
6581// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
6582// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
6583static bool ParseFlag(const char* str, const char* flag_name, bool* value) {
6584 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
6585 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag_name, true);
6586
6587 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
6588 if (value_str == nullptr) return false;
6589
6590 // Converts the string value to a bool.
6591 *value = !(*value_str == '0' || *value_str == 'f' || *value_str == 'F');
6592 return true;
6593}
6594
6595// Parses a string for an int32_t flag, in the form of "--flag=value".
6596//
6597// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
6598// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
6599bool ParseFlag(const char* str, const char* flag_name, int32_t* value) {
6600 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
6601 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag_name, false);
6602
6603 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
6604 if (value_str == nullptr) return false;
6605
6606 // Sets *value to the value of the flag.
6607 return ParseInt32(Message() << "The value of flag --" << flag_name, value_str,
6608 value);
6609}
6610
6611// Parses a string for a string flag, in the form of "--flag=value".
6612//
6613// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
6614// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
6615template <typename String>
6616static bool ParseFlag(const char* str, const char* flag_name, String* value) {
6617 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
6618 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag_name, false);
6619
6620 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
6621 if (value_str == nullptr) return false;
6622
6623 // Sets *value to the value of the flag.
6624 *value = value_str;
6625 return true;
6626}
6627
6628// Determines whether a string has a prefix that Google Test uses for its
6629// flags, i.e., starts with GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ or GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_DASH_.
6630// If Google Test detects that a command line flag has its prefix but is not
6631// recognized, it will print its help message. Flags starting with
6632// GTEST_INTERNAL_PREFIX_ followed by "internal_" are considered Google Test
6633// internal flags and do not trigger the help message.
6634static bool HasGoogleTestFlagPrefix(const char* str) {
6635 return (SkipPrefix("--", &str) || SkipPrefix("-", &str) ||
6636 SkipPrefix("/", &str)) &&
6637 !SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ "internal_", &str) &&
6638 (SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_, &str) ||
6639 SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_DASH_, &str));
6640}
6641
6642// Prints a string containing code-encoded text. The following escape
6643// sequences can be used in the string to control the text color:
6644//
6645// @@ prints a single '@' character.
6646// @R changes the color to red.
6647// @G changes the color to green.
6648// @Y changes the color to yellow.
6649// @D changes to the default terminal text color.
6650//
6651static void PrintColorEncoded(const char* str) {
6652 GTestColor color = GTestColor::kDefault; // The current color.
6653
6654 // Conceptually, we split the string into segments divided by escape
6655 // sequences. Then we print one segment at a time. At the end of
6656 // each iteration, the str pointer advances to the beginning of the
6657 // next segment.
6658 for (;;) {
6659 const char* p = strchr(str, '@');
6660 if (p == nullptr) {
6661 ColoredPrintf(color, "%s", str);
6662 return;
6663 }
6664
6665 ColoredPrintf(color, "%s", std::string(str, p).c_str());
6666
6667 const char ch = p[1];
6668 str = p + 2;
6669 if (ch == '@') {
6670 ColoredPrintf(color, "@");
6671 } else if (ch == 'D') {
6672 color = GTestColor::kDefault;
6673 } else if (ch == 'R') {
6674 color = GTestColor::kRed;
6675 } else if (ch == 'G') {
6676 color = GTestColor::kGreen;
6677 } else if (ch == 'Y') {
6678 color = GTestColor::kYellow;
6679 } else {
6680 --str;
6681 }
6682 }
6683}

6818static void LoadFlagsFromFile(const std::string& path) {
6819 FILE* flagfile = posix::FOpen(path.c_str(), "r");
6820 if (!flagfile) {
6821 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Unable to open file \"" << GTEST_FLAG_GET(flagfile)
6822 << "\"";
6823 }
6824 std::string contents(ReadEntireFile(flagfile));
6825 posix::FClose(flagfile);
6826 std::vector<std::string> lines;
6827 SplitString(contents, '\n', &lines);
6828 for (size_t i = 0; i < lines.size(); ++i) {
6829 if (lines[i].empty()) continue;
6830 if (!ParseGoogleTestFlag(lines[i].c_str())) g_help_flag = true;
6831 }
6832}
6833#endif // GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_ && GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6834
6835// Parses the command line for Google Test flags, without initializing
6836// other parts of Google Test. The type parameter CharType can be
6837// instantiated to either char or wchar_t.
6838template <typename CharType>
6839void ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnlyImpl(int* argc, CharType** argv) {
6840 std::string flagfile_value;
6841 for (int i = 1; i < *argc; i++) {
6842 const std::string arg_string = StreamableToString(argv[i]);
6843 const char* const arg = arg_string.c_str();
6844
6845 using internal::ParseFlag;
6846
6847 bool remove_flag = false;
6848 if (ParseGoogleTestFlag(arg)) {
6849 remove_flag = true;
6850#if GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_ && GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6851 } else if (ParseFlag(arg, "flagfile", &flagfile_value)) {
6852 GTEST_FLAG_SET(flagfile, flagfile_value);
6853 LoadFlagsFromFile(flagfile_value);
6854 remove_flag = true;
6855#endif // GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_ && GTEST_HAS_FILE_SYSTEM
6856 } else if (arg_string == "--help" || HasGoogleTestFlagPrefix(arg)) {
6857 // Both help flag and unrecognized Google Test flags (excluding
6858 // internal ones) trigger help display.
6859 g_help_flag = true;
6860 }
6861
6862 if (remove_flag) {
6863 // Shift the remainder of the argv list left by one.
6864 for (int j = i + 1; j < *argc; ++j) {
6865 argv[j - 1] = argv[j];
6866 }
6867
6868 // Decrements the argument count.
6869 (*argc)--;
6870
6871 // Terminate the array with nullptr.
6872 argv[*argc] = nullptr;
6873
6874 // We also need to decrement the iterator as we just removed
6875 // an element.
6876 i--;
6877 }
6878 }
6879
6880 if (g_help_flag) {
6881 // We print the help here instead of in RUN_ALL_TESTS(), as the
6882 // latter may not be called at all if the user is using Google
6883 // Test with another testing framework.
6884 PrintColorEncoded(kColorEncodedHelpMessage);
6885 }
6886}
6887
6888// Parses the command line for Google Test flags, without initializing
6889// other parts of Google Test. This function updates argc and argv by removing
6890// flags that are known to GoogleTest (including other user flags defined using
6891// ABSL_FLAG if GoogleTest is built with GTEST_USE_ABSL). Other arguments
6892// remain in place. Unrecognized flags are not reported and do not cause the
6893// program to exit.
6894void ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly(int* argc, char** argv) {
6895#ifdef GTEST_HAS_ABSL_FLAGS
6896 if (*argc <= 0) return;
6897
6898 std::vector<char*> positional_args;
6899 std::vector<absl::UnrecognizedFlag> unrecognized_flags;
6900 absl::ParseAbseilFlagsOnly(*argc, argv, positional_args, unrecognized_flags);
6901 absl::flat_hash_set<absl::string_view> unrecognized;
6902 for (const auto& flag : unrecognized_flags) {
6903 unrecognized.insert(flag.flag_name);
6904 }
6905 absl::flat_hash_set<char*> positional;
6906 for (const auto& arg : positional_args) {
6907 positional.insert(arg);
6908 }
6909
6910 int out_pos = 1;
6911 int in_pos = 1;
6912 for (; in_pos < *argc; ++in_pos) {
6913 char* arg = argv[in_pos];
6914 absl::string_view arg_str(arg);
6915 if (absl::ConsumePrefix(&arg_str, "--")) {
6916 // Flag-like argument. If the flag was unrecognized, keep it.
6917 // If it was a GoogleTest flag, remove it.
6918 if (unrecognized.contains(arg_str)) {
6919 argv[out_pos++] = argv[in_pos];
6920 continue;
6921 }
6922 }
6923
6924 if (arg_str.empty()) {
6925 ++in_pos;
6926 break; // '--' indicates that the rest of the arguments are positional
6927 }
6928
6929 // Probably a positional argument. If it is in fact positional, keep it.
6930 // If it was a value for the flag argument, remove it.
6931 if (positional.contains(arg)) {
6932 argv[out_pos++] = arg;
6933 }
6934 }
6935
6936 // The rest are positional args for sure.
6937 while (in_pos < *argc) {
6938 argv[out_pos++] = argv[in_pos++];
6939 }
6940
6941 *argc = out_pos;
6942 argv[out_pos] = nullptr;
6943#else
6944 ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnlyImpl(argc, argv);
6945#endif
6946
6947 // Fix the value of *_NSGetArgc() on macOS, but if and only if
6948 // *_NSGetArgv() == argv
6949 // Only applicable to char** version of argv
6950#ifdef GTEST_OS_MAC
6951#ifndef GTEST_OS_IOS
6952 if (*_NSGetArgv() == argv) {
6953 *_NSGetArgc() = *argc;
6954 }
6955#endif
6956#endif
6957}
6958void ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly(int* argc, wchar_t** argv) {
6959 ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnlyImpl(argc, argv);
6960}

6962// The internal implementation of InitGoogleTest().
6963//
6964// The type parameter CharType can be instantiated to either char or
6965// wchar_t.
6966template <typename CharType>
6967void InitGoogleTestImpl(int* argc, CharType** argv) {
6968 // We don't want to run the initialization code twice.
6969 if (GTestIsInitialized()) return;
6970
6971 if (*argc <= 0) return;
6972
6973 g_argvs.clear();
6974 for (int i = 0; i != *argc; i++) {
6975 g_argvs.push_back(StreamableToString(argv[i]));
6976 }
6977
6978#ifdef GTEST_HAS_ABSL
6979 absl::InitializeSymbolizer(g_argvs[0].c_str());
6980
6981#ifdef GTEST_HAS_ABSL_FLAGS
6982 // When using the Abseil Flags library, set the program usage message to the
6983 // help message, but remove the color-encoding from the message first.
6984 absl::SetProgramUsageMessage(absl::StrReplaceAll(
6985 kColorEncodedHelpMessage,
6986 {{"@D", ""}, {"@R", ""}, {"@G", ""}, {"@Y", ""}, {"@@", "@"}}));
6987#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL_FLAGS
6988#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
6989
6990 ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly(argc, argv);
6991 GetUnitTestImpl()->PostFlagParsingInit();
6992}

6996// Initializes Google Test. This must be called before calling
6997// RUN_ALL_TESTS(). In particular, it parses a command line for the
6998// flags that Google Test recognizes. Whenever a Google Test flag is
6999// seen, it is removed from argv, and *argc is decremented.
7000//
7001// No value is returned. Instead, the Google Test flag variables are
7002// updated.
7003//
7004// Calling the function for the second time has no user-visible effect.
7005void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, char** argv) {
7006#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7007 GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_(argc, argv);
7008#else // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7009 internal::InitGoogleTestImpl(argc, argv);
7010#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7011}
7012
7013// This overloaded version can be used in Windows programs compiled in
7014// UNICODE mode.
7015void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, wchar_t** argv) {
7016#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7017 GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_(argc, argv);
7018#else // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7019 internal::InitGoogleTestImpl(argc, argv);
7020#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7021}

7023// This overloaded version can be used on Arduino/embedded platforms where
7024// there is no argc/argv.
7025void InitGoogleTest() {
7026 // Since Arduino doesn't have a command line, fake out the argc/argv arguments
7027 int argc = 1;
7028 const auto arg0 = "dummy";
7029 char* argv0 = const_cast<char*>(arg0);
7030 char** argv = &argv0;
7031
7032#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7033 GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_(&argc, argv);
7034#else // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7035 internal::InitGoogleTestImpl(&argc, argv);
7036#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)

7041// Returns the value of the first environment variable that is set and contains
7042// a non-empty string. If there are none, returns the "fallback" string. Adds
7043// the director-separator character as a suffix if not provided in the
7044// environment variable value.
7045static std::string GetDirFromEnv(
7046 std::initializer_list<const char*> environment_variables,
7047 const char* fallback, char separator) {
7048 for (const char* variable_name : environment_variables) {
7049 const char* value = internal::posix::GetEnv(variable_name);
7050 if (value != nullptr && value[0] != '\0') {
7051 if (value[strlen(value) - 1] != separator) {
7052 return std::string(value).append(1, separator);
7053 }
7054 return value;
7055 }
7056 }
7057 return fallback;
7058}
7059#endif

7101// Pushes the given source file location and message onto a per-thread
7102// trace stack maintained by Google Test.
7103void ScopedTrace::PushTrace(const char* file, int line, std::string message) {
7104 internal::TraceInfo trace;
7105 trace.file = file;
7106 trace.line = line;
7107 trace.message.swap(message);
7108
7109 UnitTest::GetInstance()->PushGTestTrace(trace);
7110}

7112// Pops the info pushed by the c'tor.
7113ScopedTrace::~ScopedTrace() GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(&UnitTest::mutex_) {
7114 UnitTest::GetInstance()->PopGTestTrace();
7115}
